def display_size_refusal(*, header: Mapping[str, Any], display_size: tuple[int, int]) -> str | None:
    """Say why the replay is refused when its window did not open at the recorded size.

    Args:
        header: The recording's header fields (its ``screen_size``).
        display_size: The size the replay's display has, once opened.

    Returns:
        The refusal's message (one line, naming both sizes), or None when the sizes match or
        the recording holds no size.

    """
    recorded_size = recorded_screen_size(header=header)
    if recorded_size is None or display_size == recorded_size:
        return None
    recorded_width, recorded_height = recorded_size
    display_width, display_height = display_size
    return (
        f'it was recorded on a {recorded_width}x{recorded_height} display, but the window '
        f'opened at {display_width}x{display_height} (the window manager chose another size); '
        f'refusing to replay it'
    )

    return next(
        _sprite_differences(frame_index=frame_index, recorded=recorded, replayed=replayed), None
    )

def playback_replay_sources(
    *, header: dict[str, Any], frames: Sequence[dict[str, Any]], start: SceneStart, start_frame: int
) -> ReplaySources:
    """Return the sources an in-game playback scope serves a recording from (rule 18).

    Args:
        header: The recording's header fields (its ``random_seed`` and ``recorded_at`` are
            required).
        frames: Every recorded frame, decoded (glitchygames/tracing.py).
        start: The ``scene_start`` frame ``start_frame`` holds: the rebuilt scene's start,
            whose save view the saves start from (over the header's).
        start_frame: The recording frame served first.

    Returns:
        The sources, not installed (the scope pushes them; glitchygames/sources.py).

    Raises:
        TraceFormatError: If the header cannot be replayed, or the frames before
            ``start_frame`` are malformed (a sprite without an id or with an id that is not
            ``<Class>#<n>``, an unreadable device descriptor or input change).

    """
    header_saves: object = header.get(SAVES_HEADER_FIELD, {})
    if not isinstance(header_saves, dict):
        message = f'The recording header saves is not a mapping: {header_saves!r}'
        raise TraceFormatError(message)
    saves: dict[str, Any] = {**cast('dict[str, Any]', header_saves), **start.saves}
    first_logic_frame = start.first_logic_frame
    return decoded_replay_sources(
        header={**header, SAVES_HEADER_FIELD: saves},
        frames=frames,
        # Only recordings that hold scene starts can be played, and those are this format's
        format_version=TRACE_FORMAT_VERSION,
        # Nobody watches a playback's replay: it never holds or pauses and stops at its end
        # or first divergence (the scope ends then)
        options=ReplayOptions(
            headless=True,
            start_frame=start_frame,
            serves_redelivered_events=True,
            earlier_internal_event_count=(
                0 if first_logic_frame is None else first_logic_frame.earlier_internal_event_count
            ),
        ),
    )

    return [
        frame_index + 1
        for frame_index, frame in enumerate(frames)
        if bookmark_record in frame.get(CONTROL_EVENTS_FIELD, [])
    ]

def recorded_screen_size(*, header: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """Return the header's ``screen_size`` as (width, height), or None when it holds none.

    The engine's recorder always writes it; a header without one was made some other way (by
    hand, by a test).

    Raises:
        TraceFormatError: If the header's ``screen_size`` is not two positive integers.

    """
    screen_size: object = header.get(SCREEN_SIZE_HEADER_FIELD)
    if screen_size is None:
        return None
    match screen_size:
        case [int() as width, int() as height] if (
            not isinstance(width, bool)
            and not isinstance(height, bool)
            and width > 0
            and height > 0
        ):
            return (width, height)
        case _:
            message = (
                f'The recording header screen_size is not a positive [width, height] '
                f'(found {screen_size!r})'
            )
            raise TraceFormatError(message)

def replayed_batch_origins(*, doors: EngineSources) -> list[str] | None:
    """Return each event's origin in the doors' last batch, when a replay's merge knows them.

    A recorder over a replay (``--rebaseline``) takes them from the replay, and so does the
    instant-replay journal (glitchygames/instant_replay.py, rule 4): a watched replay's held
    frames drain the real queue between pumps, so the posts pending before a pump do not tell
    them. So does a playback scope over a replay of the session
    (glitchygames/replay/playback.py, rule 5): the replay's pump has consumed the posts, and a
    recorded external event of a type SDL never generates (a live supervisor's input post) is
    told from the replayed code's posts only by its recorded origin.

    Args:
        doors: The doors that pumped (the run's installed ones, or a recording around them).

    Returns:
        The origins, in the batch's order, or None when the doors are not a replay's.

    """
    while isinstance(doors, RecordingSources):
        doors = doors.inner
    if isinstance(doors, ReplaySources):
        return doors.last_batch_origins()
    return None

def start_replay(
    *,
    path: Path,
    game_class_name: str,
    game_module: str,
    options: dict[str, Any],
    use_fastevents: bool = False,
) -> ReplaySources:
    """Read a recording and prepare the run to replay it (rule 1); the caller installs it.

    A recording of another game raises ReplayRefusedError (``check_recorded_game``); an
    unreadable file raises TraceFormatError or OSError (``ReplaySources.from_path``). The engine
    exits with ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` on each, or ``ExitCode.MISSING_INPUT`` for a missing
    file.

    Args:
        path: The recording.
        game_class_name: The class name of the game being started.
        game_module: The module the game being started is defined in.
        options: The run's options, given the recorded ones in place; ``replay_fps`` (local, so
            never the recording's) picks the FPS source, ``RECORDED_REPLAY_FPS`` when unset, and
            ``replay_digest`` (local) the digest file (rule 12), none when unset, and
            ``headless`` (local) whether frames are paced (rule 13) and whether the replay is
            watched, starting at its start screen (rule 14) unless ``replay_pause_at_frame``
            (local) restarts it at a pause frame (rule 15; ignored, with a warning, when
            headless), ``replay_restart_handoff`` (local) where a supervised restart hands its
            own restart over (glitchygames/replay/rebuild.py), and ``replay_viewer_state``
            (local) the viewer state it starts with. ``rebaseline`` (local) makes the replay
            run on past divergences and exit ``SUCCESS`` once over (rule 17).
        use_fastevents: Drain the real queue with pygame.fastevent (``GameEngine.USE_FASTEVENTS``).

    Returns:
        The replay's sources, not yet installed.

    """
    # Local options (REPLAY_LOCAL_OPTIONS): the recorded ones applied below never replace them
    replay_digest = options.get('replay_digest')
    headless = bool(options.get('headless'))
    pause_at_frame = options.get('replay_pause_at_frame')
    if pause_at_frame is not None and headless:
        LOG.warning(
            '--replay-pause-at-frame is ignored with --headless: nobody could unpause the replay'
        )
        pause_at_frame = None
    restart_handoff = options.get('replay_restart_handoff')
    is_rebaseline = options.get('rebaseline') is not None
    replay_options = ReplayOptions(
        headless=headless,
        # A rebaseline writes the new recording whatever the result (rule 17)
        exit_policy=(
            ReplayExitPolicy.SUCCESS_AFTER_WRITING if is_rebaseline else ReplayExitPolicy.RESULT
        ),
        fps_source=options.get('replay_fps') or RECORDED_REPLAY_FPS,
        digest_path=None if replay_digest is None else Path(replay_digest),
        use_fastevents=use_fastevents,
        # Every watched replay starts at its start screen (rule 14), but a restart: the viewer
        # already started it (rule 15)
        wait_for_start=not headless and pause_at_frame is None,
        pause_at_frame=pause_at_frame,
        restart_handoff_path=None if restart_handoff is None else Path(restart_handoff),
        viewer_state=options.get('replay_viewer_state'),
        recording_path=path,
        # A rebaseline summarizes every frame that changed, so it never stops at the first
        stop_on_divergence=not is_rebaseline,
        # The rebaseline's new recording holds the scene starts, frame 0's included (rule 17)
        captures_scene_starts=is_rebaseline,
        # --max-processing-slowdown implies --compare-processing (replay/processing.py)
        compare_processing=bool(options.get('compare_processing'))
        or options.get('max_processing_slowdown') is not None,
        max_processing_slowdown_percent=options.get('max_processing_slowdown'),
    )
    sources = ReplaySources.from_path(path=path, options=replay_options)
    check_recorded_game(
        header=sources.header, game_class_name=game_class_name, game_module=game_module
    )
    recorded_version = sources.header.get(ENGINE_VERSION_HEADER_FIELD)
    installed_version = installed_engine_version()
    if recorded_version != installed_version:
        LOG.warning(
            'The recording was made with engine version %s; this is %s. The replay may diverge',
            recorded_version,
            installed_version,
        )
    apply_recorded_options(options=options, recorded=sources.header.get(OPTIONS_HEADER_FIELD, {}))
    apply_recorded_screen_size(
        options=options, screen_size=recorded_screen_size(header=sources.header)
    )
    seed_engine_random(seed=sources.random_seed)
    if replay_options.fps_source == REAL_REPLAY_FPS:
        LOG.warning(REAL_REPLAY_FPS_NOTICE)
    return sources

write_bookmarked_copy(*, recording_path, bookmarks, destination) #

Write a copy of a recording with a breakpoint for each bookmark (rule 16).

The recording's header and complete frames are copied as read; for each bookmark N, frame N - 1 gets BOOKMARK_CONTROL_EVENT appended to its control events, unless it already has it, and its newest content hash (content_hash[0], glitchygames/recording_history.py) is recomputed to describe the breakpoint. The header gains bookmarked_copy_of (the source's file name, kept from a copy), source_truncated when the source was cut off, and input_capture_format_version when the source is older than format version 3, so the copy replays as its source does. A copy an earlier session saved from the same source keeps its bookmarks: they are added to bookmarks (a copy of another recording is never written over). The copy is written aside, then moved into place (glitchygames.output_files.write_aside_then_replace), so destination is never left half written, even when it is recording_path.

Parameters:
  • recording_path (Path) –

    The recording to copy (never written, unless it is a bookmarked copy and destination).

  • bookmarks (list[int]) –

    The bookmarked frames (ReplayControls.bookmarks), each 1 to the recording's frame count.

  • destination (Path) –

    The copy's path (bookmarked_copy_path): a new file or a bookmarked copy.
Raises:
  • ValueError –

    If destination exists but is not a bookmarked copy of recording_path, or a bookmark is outside the recording (nothing is written either way).

    The recording's header and complete frames are copied as read; for each bookmark N, frame
    N - 1 gets ``BOOKMARK_CONTROL_EVENT`` appended to its control events, unless it already has
    it, and its newest content hash (``content_hash[0]``, glitchygames/recording_history.py)
    is recomputed to describe the breakpoint. The header gains ``bookmarked_copy_of`` (the
    source's file name, kept from a copy), ``source_truncated`` when the source was cut off,
    and ``input_capture_format_version`` when the source is older than format version 3, so
    the copy replays as its source does. A
    copy an earlier session saved from the same source keeps its bookmarks: they are added to
    ``bookmarks`` (a copy of another recording is never written over). The copy is written
    aside, then moved into place (``glitchygames.output_files.write_aside_then_replace``), so
    ``destination`` is never left half written, even when it is ``recording_path``.

    Args:
        recording_path: The recording to copy (never written, unless it is a bookmarked copy
            and ``destination``).
        bookmarks: The bookmarked frames (``ReplayControls.bookmarks``), each 1 to the
            recording's frame count.
        destination: The copy's path (``bookmarked_copy_path``): a new file or a bookmarked
            copy.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``destination`` exists but is not a bookmarked copy of
            ``recording_path``, or a bookmark is outside the recording (nothing is written
            either way).

    """
    bookmarks = sorted({
        *bookmarks,
        *_earlier_copy_bookmarks(recording_path=recording_path, destination=destination),
    })
    read_result = read_trace_result(path=recording_path)
    trace = read_result.trace
    frames: list[dict[str, Any]] = trace[FRAMES_FIELD]
    bookmark_record = BOOKMARK_CONTROL_EVENT.to_json()
    for bookmark in bookmarks:
        if not 1 <= bookmark <= len(frames):
            message = (
                f'Bookmark {bookmark} is outside the recording {recording_path} '
                f'(frames 1 to {len(frames)} can be bookmarked)'
            )
            raise ValueError(message)
        frame = frames[bookmark - 1]
        control_events = list(frame.get(CONTROL_EVENTS_FIELD, []))
        if bookmark_record not in control_events:
            control_events.append(bookmark_record)
        frame[CONTROL_EVENTS_FIELD] = control_events
        # The breakpoint is the frame's content now (a rebaseline of the copy re-applies it), so
        # the newest run's hash describes it; older runs' hashes stay as they were
        recorded_hashes = frame.get(CONTENT_HASH_FIELD)
        if isinstance(recorded_hashes, list) and recorded_hashes:
            frame[CONTENT_HASH_FIELD] = [
                frame_content_hash(frame_record=frame),
                *cast('list[Any]', recorded_hashes)[1:],
            ]
    trace.setdefault(BOOKMARKED_COPY_OF_HEADER_FIELD, recording_path.name)
    if is_cut_off(read_result=read_result):
        trace[SOURCE_TRUNCATED_HEADER_FIELD] = True
    if read_result.format_version < TRACE_FORMAT_VERSION:
        trace.setdefault(INPUT_CAPTURE_FORMAT_HEADER_FIELD, read_result.format_version)
    write_aside_then_replace(
        destination=destination, write=lambda aside: write_trace(trace=trace, path=aside)
    )

ghosts #

Ghosts: one sprite's recorded path and looks, drawn beside live play (a time-trial ghost).

A ghost is appearance, not play (plans/2026-10-19-gameplay-replay.md, section 5.5). The rules:

  1. Recording: GhostRecorder(sprite=..., scene=...) is a supervisor (glitchygames/supervision.py); it registers itself with SceneManager().add_supervisor as it is made and removes itself in finish(), which returns the GhostTrack. At each frame's supervisor slot (after the frame's logic and events, before the camera aim and positioning) it keeps one GhostSample: the scene's game_time, the sprite's world_x/world_y, its appearance(sprite) (default_appearance: animation, frame, horizontal flip and draw offset of an AnimatedSprite; kept as a read-only copy) and whether the game shows it (not hidden for a world-space sprite: its visible is the engine's culling, which says where the camera was, not whether the sprite was shown; visible for any other sprite).
  2. Only live frames of its scene are sampled: frames whose active scene is the scene it was given (another scene has its own game time), in which that scene's game time advanced (not behind the pause screen, not the frame a resume switches back to it), and never inside a playback scope (a demo or an instant replay plays a rebuilt scene; glitchygames/replay/playback.py). A recorder made while a scope plays (by the rebuilt scene's setup(), say) belongs to the scope: the scene manager removes it when the scope ends (glitchygames/supervision.py), and it samples nothing. A recorder stays registered until finish(), even once its scene is gone: a scene left (for the pause screen, or for another the game comes back from) may return, so the engine cannot tell it is over; a recorder never finished samples nothing more, but is kept (with its scene) until the game calls finish(), typically when the run it records ends. The recorder reads game state only: it draws no randomness, posts no event and records no control event, so recording a ghost changes nothing a --record-trace recording holds or a replay compares.
  3. Timing: samples are keyed by Scene.game_time, the sum of the scene's (capped) dt since it started, which stops while the scene is paused. A ghost drawn in a later run of the same scene shows, at each moment, the last sample not after that run's game_time (GhostTrack.sample_at), so it lines up with the live run from the scene's start whatever the frame rate, and stands still while the game is paused. With the same dt every frame, the ghost is drawn exactly where the recorded sprite was drawn.
  4. Storing: GhostTrack.to_json() / from_json() (frozen pydantic models; unknown fields are refused). The game stores tracks, typically in its saves (glitchygames.state. open_saves): a replay serves the saves the recording saw (a sandbox), so the replayed ghost is the recorded one. A track read from anywhere else must be the same file when the session is replayed.
  5. Drawing: GhostSprite(track=..., image_for=...) is a world-space sprite (COORDINATE_SPACE = CoordinateSpace.WORLD): the engine positions and culls it like any world sprite and is the only writer of its rect's position. The game sets ghost.scene to the scene it adds the ghost to (whose game_time it follows) and adds it to the scene's all_sprites. Its world_x, world_y and draw_offset are read from the track at the scene's current game_time whenever they are read, and that read brings its image and rect size up to date, so the engine's positioning (which runs before update()) places and culls this frame's sample, never the last frame's. Its image is image_for(sample) as a translucent copy (alpha), made once per distinct appearance (keyed by the appearance's JSON), and the rect takes its size (its top-left stays the engine's). With nothing to show (no scene, before the track's first sample, or a sample that is not visible) its image is empty (0 x 0), which the engine's culling hides (visible 0). hidden is the game's own flag only, as for every world sprite (set hidden = True to hide it, never visible = False), so saving and restoring it is safe. It has no hitbox: never add it to a collision group.
  6. In traces: a ghost in all_sprites is sampled like every sprite (its rect and visible), and it is deterministic: its track comes from saves (rule 4) and its position from the replayed game_time, so a session with a ghost replays without divergence. Inside an instant replay the rebuilt scene adds its own ghost as the live scene did (from the sandboxed saves), following its own game_time.

class GhostRecorder:
    """A supervisor that samples one sprite once per live frame of its scene (module rules 1-2)."""

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        *,
        sprite: WorldPositioned,
        scene: Scene,
        appearance: Callable[[object], dict[str, Any]] = default_appearance,
    ) -> None:
        """Start recording ``sprite``: register with the scene manager's supervisor slot.

        Args:
            sprite: The sprite to record (it has world_x and world_y).
            scene: The scene the sprite plays in: only its frames are sampled, keyed by its
                game time.
            appearance: Returns the JSON-safe looks of the sprite for each sample.

        """
        self._sprite = sprite
        self._scene = scene
        self._appearance = appearance
        self._samples: list[GhostSample] = []
        self._track: GhostTrack | None = None
        SceneManager().add_supervisor(supervisor=self)

    def on_frame(self: Self, *, frame_number: int, scene: Scene | None) -> None:
        """Sample the sprite, if this frame ran the recorded scene's logic live.

        Args:
            frame_number: The frame being run (unused: samples are keyed by game time).
            scene: The active scene at the supervisor slot.

        """
        del frame_number
        # A supervisor earlier in the slot may have finished this recorder this frame
        if self._track is not None or scene is not self._scene:
            return
        if SceneManager().in_playback_scope:
            return
        game_seconds = self._scene.game_time
        if self._samples and game_seconds <= self._samples[-1].game_seconds:
            return
        sprite = self._sprite
        if is_world_positioned(sprite):
            shown = not getattr(sprite, 'hidden', False)
        else:
            shown = bool(getattr(sprite, 'visible', True))
        self._samples.append(
            GhostSample(
                game_seconds=game_seconds,
                world_x=sprite.world_x,
                world_y=sprite.world_y,
                appearance=self._appearance(sprite),
                visible=shown,
            )
        )

    def finish(self: Self) -> GhostTrack:
        """Stop recording: leave the supervisor slot and return the track (the same each call).

        Returns:
            The recorded track.

        """
        if self._track is None:
            SceneManager().remove_supervisor(supervisor=self)
            self._track = GhostTrack(samples=tuple(self._samples))
        return self._track

class GhostSample(BaseModel):
    """Where and how the recorded sprite was drawn at one moment of its scene's game time."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra='forbid')

    # Scene.game_time when the sample was taken (after that frame's logic)
    game_seconds: float
    world_x: float
    world_y: float
    # JSON-safe; default_appearance's keys unless the recorder was given another function.
    # Kept read-only (mappings read-only, lists as tuples): its JSON keys a ghost's image cache
    appearance: Mapping[str, Any]
    # Whether the game showed the sprite (not hidden); the ghost draws nothing when False
    visible: bool

    @field_validator('appearance', mode='before')
    @classmethod
    def _appearance_is_a_mapping(cls, appearance: object) -> object:
        """Refuse an appearance that is not a mapping, naming what an appearance must be.

        A custom ``appearance`` function (GhostRecorder) is the usual source of a wrong value.

        Returns:
            The appearance, for pydantic's own validation.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the appearance is not a mapping.

        """
        if isinstance(appearance, Mapping):
            return cast('Mapping[str, Any]', appearance)
        message = (
            f'A ghost appearance must be a mapping of JSON values, got {type(appearance).__name__}'
        )
        # A ValueError, not a TypeError: pydantic turns only ValueError (and AssertionError)
        # raised by a validator into a ValidationError
        raise ValueError(message)

    @field_validator('appearance', mode='after')
    @classmethod
    def _read_only_appearance(cls, appearance: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
        """Keep a read-only copy of the appearance given, so nobody can change it later.

        Pydantic validates a ``Mapping`` field into a new dict, so the copy is made after it.

        Returns:
            The read-only copy.

        """
        return frozen_json_value(appearance)

    @field_serializer('appearance')
    def _plain_appearance(self: Self, appearance: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Write the appearance as plain JSON types (dicts and lists).

        Returns:
            The plain copy.

        """
        return thawed_json_value(appearance)

class GhostSprite(pygame.sprite.DirtySprite):
    """A translucent world-space sprite that plays a ``GhostTrack`` (module rules 3, 5 and 6).

    Set ``scene`` to the scene the ghost is added to; until then it draws nothing.
    """

    COORDINATE_SPACE = CoordinateSpace.WORLD

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        *,
        track: GhostTrack,
        image_for: Callable[[GhostSample], pygame.Surface],
        alpha: int = DEFAULT_GHOST_ALPHA,
    ) -> None:
        """Create a ghost with no image yet; it draws once its scene reaches the first sample.

        Args:
            track: The recorded track.
            image_for: Returns the image for a sample (``images_from_animated_sprite``); called
                once per distinct appearance.
            alpha: How opaque the ghost is drawn (0-255).

        """
        super().__init__()
        self.scene: GameTimed | None = None
        self._track = track
        self._image_for = image_for
        self._alpha = alpha
        # The game's own flag, as for every world sprite (the engine's culling reads it)
        self.hidden = False
        # The scene and game time the current sample was looked up for
        self._looked_up_for: tuple[GameTimed, float] | None = None
        self._sample: GhostSample | None = None
        # The JSON of the appearance drawn, or None while the empty image is shown
        self._drawn_appearance: str | None = None
        self._images_by_appearance: dict[str, pygame.Surface] = {}
        self._empty_image = pygame.Surface((0, 0))
        self.image = self._empty_image
        self.rect = self._empty_image.get_rect()

    def _current_sample(self: Self) -> GhostSample | None:
        """Return the sample for the scene's current game time, showing its image.

        Returns:
            The sample, or None without a scene or before the track's first sample.

        """
        scene = self.scene
        if scene is None:
            self._sample = None
            self._looked_up_for = None
            self._show_image(appearance_key=None, sample=None)
            return None
        game_seconds = scene.game_time
        looked_up_for = self._looked_up_for
        if (
            looked_up_for is not None
            and looked_up_for[0] is scene
            and looked_up_for[1] == game_seconds
        ):
            return self._sample
        self._looked_up_for = (scene, game_seconds)
        sample = self._track.sample_at(game_seconds=game_seconds)
        self._sample = sample
        if sample is None or not sample.visible:
            self._show_image(appearance_key=None, sample=None)
        else:
            appearance_key = json.dumps(thawed_json_value(sample.appearance), sort_keys=True)
            self._show_image(appearance_key=appearance_key, sample=sample)
        return sample

    def _show_image(self: Self, *, appearance_key: str | None, sample: GhostSample | None) -> None:
        """Show a sample's image, made translucent once per appearance, or the empty image.

        Args:
            appearance_key: The JSON of the sample's appearance, or None for the empty image.
            sample: The sample to draw (None for the empty image).

        """
        if appearance_key == self._drawn_appearance:
            return
        if appearance_key is None or sample is None:
            image = self._empty_image
        else:
            cached_image = self._images_by_appearance.get(appearance_key)
            if cached_image is None:
                cached_image = self._image_for(sample).copy()
                cached_image.set_alpha(self._alpha)
                self._images_by_appearance[appearance_key] = cached_image
            image = cached_image
        self._drawn_appearance = appearance_key
        self.image = image
        # The size follows the image; the engine owns the position (rect.topleft)
        rect = self.rect
        assert rect is not None  # made in __init__
        rect.size = image.get_size()
        if self.dirty == 0:
            self.dirty = 1

    @property
    def world_x(self: Self) -> float:
        """World X of the sample at the scene's game time (0.0 without one)."""
        sample = self._current_sample()
        return 0.0 if sample is None else sample.world_x

    @property
    def world_y(self: Self) -> float:
        """World Y of the sample at the scene's game time (0.0 without one)."""
        sample = self._current_sample()
        return 0.0 if sample is None else sample.world_y

    @property
    def draw_offset(self: Self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """The sample's ``draw_offset`` appearance (a frame anchor's offset), else (0, 0)."""
        sample = self._current_sample()
        if sample is None or 'draw_offset' not in sample.appearance:
            return (0, 0)
        draw_offset_x, draw_offset_y = sample.appearance['draw_offset']
        return (int(draw_offset_x), int(draw_offset_y))

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Bring the image up to the scene's game time (the properties are always current)."""
        self._current_sample()

    def update_nested_sprites(self: Self) -> None:
        """Do nothing: Scene.update() calls this on every sprite, and a ghost has none."""

class GhostTrack(BaseModel):
    """A recorded sprite's samples, in game-time order."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra='forbid')

    samples: tuple[GhostSample, ...]

    @model_validator(mode='after')
    def _check_time_order(self: Self) -> Self:
        """Refuse samples whose game times go backwards (sample_at searches them).

        Returns:
            The track.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a sample's game time is earlier than the one before it.

        """
        for earlier, later in zip(self.samples, self.samples[1:], strict=False):
            if later.game_seconds < earlier.game_seconds:
                message = (
                    f'Ghost samples must be in time order: {later.game_seconds} follows '
                    f'{earlier.game_seconds}'
                )
                raise ValueError(message)
        return self

    def sample_at(self: Self, *, game_seconds: float) -> GhostSample | None:
        """Return the last sample taken at or before a game time.

        Args:
            game_seconds: The game time of the scene the ghost is drawn in.

        Returns:
            The sample, or None before the first sample (or for an empty track).

        """
        index = bisect.bisect_right(
            self.samples, game_seconds, key=lambda sample: sample.game_seconds
        )
        if index == 0:
            return None
        return self.samples[index - 1]

    def to_json(self: Self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the track as plain JSON types (for saves).

        Returns:
            ``{'samples': [...]}``, each sample a dict of its fields.

        """
        return self.model_dump(mode='json')

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, record: dict[str, Any]) -> GhostTrack:
        """Read a track written by ``to_json``.

        Args:
            record: The JSON record.

        Returns:
            The track.

        """
        return cls.model_validate(record)

def default_appearance(sprite: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return what a ghost needs to draw an ``AnimatedSprite`` as it looks now.

    Args:
        sprite: The recorded sprite.

    Returns:
        For an ``AnimatedSprite``: its ``animation`` name, ``frame`` index, ``flip_x``
        (``hitbox_flip_x``, set by games that draw it facing left) and ``draw_offset`` (its
        frame anchor's offset, as a list). For any other sprite: ``{}``.

    """
    if not isinstance(sprite, AnimatedSprite):
        return {}
    draw_offset_x, draw_offset_y = sprite.draw_offset
    return {
        'animation': sprite.current_animation,
        'frame': sprite.current_frame,
        'flip_x': bool(sprite.hitbox_flip_x),
        'draw_offset': [draw_offset_x, draw_offset_y],
    }

def images_from_animated_sprite(source: AnimatedSprite) -> Callable[[GhostSample], pygame.Surface]:
    """Return an ``image_for`` that draws a sample with an animated sprite's frames.

    The image is the frame the sample names (``default_appearance``'s ``animation`` and
    ``frame``), flipped horizontally when its ``flip_x`` is true. It is the frame as authored:
    a game that draws its sprite scaled or recoloured passes its own ``image_for``.

    Args:
        source: A sprite with the recorded sprite's animations (the same TOML, say).

    Returns:
        The function a ``GhostSprite`` draws its image with.

    """

    def image_for(sample: GhostSample) -> pygame.Surface:
        """Return the sampled frame's image.

        Returns:
            The frame's surface (a flipped copy when the sample is flipped).

        """
        appearance = sample.appearance
        frames = source.frames[str(appearance['animation'])]
        image = frames[int(appearance['frame'])].image
        if appearance.get('flip_x', False):
            return pygame.transform.flip(image, flip_x=True, flip_y=False)
        return image

    return image_for

input_blocking #

Block real input at SDL while recorded input is served, then put the earlier state back.

A replay (glitchygames/replay/driver.py) serves every external event from its recording, so real input, device and window events are blocked at SDL (pygame.event.set_blocked): they never enter the queue. EventTypeBlock records each type's blocked state before blocking it and restores exactly that state, so a type a game had already blocked stays blocked. Event managers made mid-run (a scene's widgets) call pygame.event.set_allowed, so the replay blocks the types again on every pump (reassert). Part 3's playback scope can reuse it.

Blocking a type also refuses posts of it (pygame.event.post returns False), including the game's own: game code that fakes input by posting, say, KEYDOWN loses those posts during a replay. The engine's own posts are QUIT and custom types, which are never blocked.

EventTypeBlock #

Blocks event types at SDL and restores each one's blocked state at block() time.

restore() returns every type to the state it had when block() ran, overriding any pygame.event.set_allowed or set_blocked calls made for those types in between.

class EventTypeBlock:
    """Blocks event types at SDL and restores each one's blocked state at ``block()`` time.

    ``restore()`` returns every type to the state it had when ``block()`` ran, overriding any
    ``pygame.event.set_allowed`` or ``set_blocked`` calls made for those types in between.

    Attributes:
        event_types: The types ``block()`` blocks.

    """

    def __init__(self: Self, *, event_types: Iterable[int]) -> None:
        """Prepare to block ``event_types`` (nothing is blocked until ``block()``).

        Args:
            event_types: The event types to block.

        """
        self.event_types: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(event_types)
        # Type -> whether it was blocked before block(); None while not active
        self._blocked_before: dict[int, bool] | None = None

    @property
    def is_active(self: Self) -> bool:
        """True between ``block()`` and ``restore()``."""
        return self._blocked_before is not None

    def block(self: Self) -> None:
        """Record each type's blocked state, then block every type (a no-op while active)."""
        if self.is_active:
            return
        self._blocked_before = {
            event_type: pygame.event.get_blocked(event_type) for event_type in self.event_types
        }
        pygame.event.set_blocked(list(self.event_types))

    def reassert(self: Self) -> None:
        """Block every type again, keeping the snapshot ``block()`` took (a no-op unless active).

        Undoes ``pygame.event.set_allowed`` calls made since (an event manager made mid-run).
        """
        if self._blocked_before is None:
            return
        pygame.event.set_blocked(list(self.event_types))

    def restore(self: Self) -> None:
        """Return each type to its state at ``block()`` time (a no-op unless active).

        Types blocked then stay blocked; the others are unblocked, whatever was set in between.
        """
        if self._blocked_before is None:
            return
        pygame.event.set_allowed([
            event_type
            for event_type, was_blocked in self._blocked_before.items()
            if not was_blocked
        ])
        self._blocked_before = None

playback #

In-game playback: a running game plays a recording to a rebuilt scene, then goes on.

Demos and instant replays run inside a playback scope, not a new engine run (plans/2026-10-19-gameplay-replay.md, section 5.2). The rules:

  1. Starting (start_playback; start_playback_from_recording reads a file first): the frame played first (PlaybackOptions.start_frame) must hold a scene_start (glitchygames/scene_start.py) with its first logic frame (rule 7 there: a recording writes a start on the scene's first logic frame, so the start's frame is where its logic began), and its scene class must be found among the loaded Scene subclasses (find_scene_class: by module and qualified name, else, where the modules cannot be compared (none recorded, or __main__ on either side), by a name no other such scene shares); otherwise nothing starts (logged; False), as for a recording that cannot be replayed (a malformed one included). The replay sources are made (playback_replay_sources, rule 18 of glitchygames/replay/driver.py) and the scope is requested (SceneManager. request_playback): the scene manager enters it at the start of the next frame, so the rebuilt scene's first frame is a whole frame, as recorded, and the frame that asked ends on the live doors. A request made while a transition plays waits for its end. A request made in a frame whose end switches scenes (next_scene) is dropped, logged: the scene to return to has gone. Scopes do not nest: inside a scope, a request is answered with the answer the frame being played recorded (an instant-replay journal's playback_answers) and requests nothing, or, without one, refused (answered_playback_request; glitchygames/instant_replay.py, rule 8).
  2. Entering (SceneManager._enter_playback): the random streams, the frame clock, the FPS event timer and the scene manager's previous_scene are saved (PlaybackRequest.begin_session); the live scene is stashed without cleanup(); PlaybackSources are pushed on top of the installed doors (push_scoped_sources; glitchygames/sources.py); a playback control event is recorded (a marker: replaying the session starts the scope again from the recorded input, so it is compared, never applied again); the scene is rebuilt (rebuild_scene) and made active as a switch would, a transition's arrival step is repeated for a scene that arrived by one; then the streams, the frame clock and the FPS event timer are set as the scene's first logic frame began, the frame takes the recording's dt, and the current polled input becomes the recording's before that frame (idle before frame 0), so the live input never leaks in.
  3. Frames: PlaybackSources serve the recording to the scene (rule 5) and the scene manager runs every frame as always, paced and presented by the installed doors (a demo plays at the game's speed), but for the fast-forwarded frames (rule 6).
  4. Ending: after each frame, the scope ends when its doors found a reason (PlaybackSources.end_reason): the player's press (exit_on_input: any key or button, PLAYBACK_EXIT_EVENT_TYPES), the recording's quit (its window's QUIT or the playback scene's own quit_game(): the scope ends, the game does not quit), the game's request (SceneManager.end_playback, 'ended_by_game': from a supervisor, the scope ends once that frame ended; between frames, at once; from the played scene's own code, ignored, as its original call did nothing), or the recording's end or divergence (the replay stops there; a playback never pauses). An error in the scope's part of a frame (its frame, the comparison, or entering) ends it too, logged (SceneManager._run_frame contains it); an error of the installed doors (a session recorder that cannot write) propagates as it would outside a scope. The run's end (SceneManager.terminate, after the player's QUIT) ends a scope in progress first and drops a requested one, so the live scene is the one torn down. Ending (SceneManager._exit_playback) keeps the replay's result (SceneManager.last_playback_result) and a PlaybackOutcome (SceneManager.last_playback_outcome: the kind, the reason and the frames played), cleans up the playback's scene, removes every supervisor and control event handler the scope's code added while it played (the rebuilt scene's setup(), event handlers or cleanup() may add one, a ghost recorder say: SceneManager.add_supervisor gives it to the scope; those added before the scope began, or by the live game's own supervisors and handlers while it played, stay; SceneManager.in_playback_scope, true while the scoped doors are pushed, is the one answer to "is a scope playing"), pops the scoped doors, restores the streams, the frame clock, the FPS event timer, the scene manager's previous_scene, its rumble controller (rule 8) and the live polled input (the installed doors' latest snapshot), posts again the live game's posts the scope drained and hands back the player's held events (rule 5), drops the playback scene's own posts still queued (made after its frame's last pump: in update(), an event handler, a supervisor or handler the scope owns, its cleanup; sources.discard_scope_posts: they stop being pending posts, and the live doors' next read of SDL's queue loses them before a recording, the instant-replay journal or the game sees the batch; a replay of the session drops them the same way as its playback scene posts them again), posts again, in posting order, the posts the live game's own supervisors and handlers made while it played (held_live_game_posts and those still queued, made in its last frame: a supervisor that calls end_playback() and then posts for the live game, say; the queued copies are dropped as the scope's are, so each arrives once, after the held events, at the live doors' next pump; pending then, a later instant replay across the scope serves them uncompared as its resume bridge's earlier events), then makes the live scene active again exactly as it was (no setup() again: only its snap mode, event proxies, caption and a full redraw), or switches to then when that is another scene. The frame that ends the scope still finishes afterwards, so the restored live frame clock resumes one frame later (it advances by that frame's dt).

  5. The scoped doors (PlaybackSources):

  6. pump_events: the installed doors pump once per pump of the frame (the real queue live; the session's recorded batch when the session is replayed, so the exit press replays too). Their batch is sorted with the internal-post tracker. The player's QUIT (and one the live game posted) is kept: it quits the game. Internal events, the playback scene's own posts, go to the replay (ReplaySources.pump_events(real_events=...)), which matches them with the recorded ones. Internal events posted before the scope began (the live game's last FPS event, say: they are the live game's, and would be divergences of the recording's first frame) are held, as are the external events the live game must not lose (releases, device and window events, PLAYBACK_HELD_EVENT_TYPES): one list (held_live_events), in the order they were pumped, each with its origin, delivered in that order before the first pump after the scope (sources.redeliver_events; a recording writes them into that frame's redelivered_events). Events still waiting to be redelivered when a scope begins (a demo that ended into a scene starting the next one) are taken into the new scope's list first, so they reach the live game, never a playback scene. When the run ends during a scope (terminate) they are dropped: no frame follows to deliver them. The posts the live game's own supervisors and control event handlers make while the scope plays (recording.live_game_posts: post_event marks them while SceneManager runs live code in a scope, rule 4; the played recording never held them) are held apart (held_live_game_posts) and posted again as the scope ends (rule 4). The live game's input posts (recording.post_input_event: a supervisor or tool standing in for the player) of an SDL type (below USEREVENT), made during the scope or before it, are the player's input (BUGS.md #196): a press reaches the exit check (it ends a demo), releases, device and window events are held with the player's (held_live_events, external), and the rest reach nothing. A replay of the session runs without the poster and serves those events from the recording as the player's, so the two agree. Its input posts of a type SDL never generates (no player makes one: a game event, a menu event, any custom_type()) are held as its other posts are, and posted (or redelivered) as input again after the scope. A replay of the session serves those from the recording too (external), and the scope holds a served event of such a type that matches no post the same way, told by its recorded origin (replayed_batch_origins: the type alone would call it internal), so it reaches the live game after the scope there as well. The rule: a supervisor may post any event (post_input_event); input of an SDL type during a scope counts as the player's; everything else reaches the game (after the scope if one is playing), live and replayed alike. The scope's code's own input posts (a supervisor the played scene added again) are dropped: the recording holds them as external and the replay serves them, so each arrives once. External events reach only the exit check, never the scene; presses and motion are dropped. The batch is the replay's (recorded external events, matched internal ones) without any QUIT (a QUIT in it ends the scope: recording_quit), then the kept QUIT.

  7. input_snapshot: the installed doors' snapshot is read (a recording of the session records the player's polled input; it is kept as last_base_snapshot), the replay's is returned.
  8. frame_seconds: the replay's (the recording's dt; past its end, the installed doors' measurement), asked after the installed doors were asked as always. Their answer is kept (installed_frame_seconds) for their end_frame.
  9. saves, devices, wall_clock_time, random_seed, opened_save_namespaces: the replay's (saves are a sandbox seeded from the scene start's save view: real saves are never touched).
  10. control_events_for_frame: the installed doors' (a replay of the session re-applies its breakpoints on the scope's frames too); the played recording's re-applied control events are never applied again (they were applied in the session that recorded them) and never compared (glitchygames/replay/driver.py, rule 8).
  11. end_frame is compare_frame (the replay compares the frame, its playback marker left out: the recording never holds it), then the installed doors' end_frame (a recording of the session writes it; glitchygames/recording.py, Playback scopes) with their own frame time (installed_frame_seconds), not the played recording's dt the frame ran with: the scope's first frame's time was read as the live frame before it ended, on the installed doors, and advanced the live frame clock and FPS event timer there, so a replay of the session must be served that time as that frame ends (BUGS.md #196). The scene manager calls the two itself, so only the comparison's errors end the scope.
  12. captures_scene_starts is True; stop_requested, pacing, holding, presenting and the overlay are the installed doors' (the scope never stops the run), except while fast-forwarding (rule 6).
  13. Fast-forward (PlaybackOptions.fast_forward_frames): the scope's first N frames run in full but unseen and unheard. While PlaybackSources.is_fast_forwarding (fewer frames compared than N), presents_frames is False and paced_frame_seconds() is 0.0, the doors a headless replay uses (the scene manager neither presents nor waits; the next presented frame updates the whole display), and after each such frame every sound it started is stopped and music is paused (FrameSilencer, glitchygames/replay/silence.py, the code path a restarted replay's rebuild uses; it follows the game's own music pauses from the scope's start, and the live game's sounds playing then play on, live voices aside). After the Nth frame the silence ends (music the silencer paused plays on, unless the game paused it) and the frames play as rule 3 says, heard as the game plays them; so does a scope that ends during the fast-forward. Music is the one mixer's: the scope neither saves nor restores it, so music the playback's scene starts or stops is the live game's too. The scope's first frame is paced as the live doors pace it (the loop asks before the frame enters the scope). None of this changes what a frame does, so a recording or replay of the session (watched or headless) is unchanged.
  14. Instant replay (SceneManager.instant_replay, start_instant_replay): the active scene's instant-replay journal (glitchygames/instant_replay.py) plays in a scope of kind 'instant' from its start_frame, returning to the scene shown (the journal's scene, or the pause screen presenting it), with no exit on input: the player's presses reach nothing, and the game decides when it ends (the journal's end, or SceneManager.end_playback from a supervisor, which reads the player's polled input from SceneManager.playback_player_input). The frames before the last Scene.INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS of frame time are fast-forwarded (fast_forward_frame_count); the rest are shown at the game's pace. Frame time, not game time: the shown part takes that long to watch, a paused stretch in it included. Refused (False, nothing starts) when the scene keeps no journal (it does not offer instant replay, its first logic frame has not run, or a scope plays) or the journal holds more frame time than Scene.MAX_INSTANT_REPLAY_FAST_FORWARD_SECONDS. The request is answered as any playback request is (rule 1: a playback of the journal gets the recorded answer and requests nothing), so a scene that asks after every goal plays back across its earlier replays. The journal's recording is taken as the request is made: the frame that asks is not in it (it ends live, before the scope begins).
  15. Rumble and live voices: a playback never rumbles the player's real controllers, neither while fast-forwarding nor in the frames it shows (a demo's crash buzzing the player's hands would be the playback's, not the game's). While a scope plays, SceneManager.rumble is a rumble controller of its own (the playback scene's pulses, sustained levels and shakes go there and reach no device); the live game's controller waits untouched and is back when the scope ends, so a playback's pulse never carries into live play. The live scene's synth voices (and those of the scene the scope returns to, and of the previous scene as it began: the game behind a pause screen an instant replay began from) pause behind the scope and play on after it (LiveAudio.update's paused_owners), even when the playback's own scene switches change previous_scene; the playback scene's own voices end with it.

Limits: a live supervisor that posts with post_event (the game's own posts, which a replay expects the replayed code to make again) during a scope makes a session that a --replay-trace replay without that supervisor cannot match. Supervisors post with post_input_event, which replays without them, whatever the event's type (rule 5). A scope that fast-forwards inside a restarted replay's rebuild silences on top of the rebuild's silence: the end of its fast-forward may resume music during the rebuild (which pauses it again after the next frame). A scene must be rebuildable from its start (Scene.replay_arguments). Of a scene that arrived by a transition, the arrival step is repeated, but the events the ride delivered to it (releases, window and device events) are not: a scene they change diverges. The first logic frame's earlier posts are counted from the internal-post tracker, so they are exact while posts are tracked (while recording or replaying, and from the first setup of a scene that keeps an instant-replay journal: glitchygames/instant_replay.py, whose JournalRecording a scope plays from its start_frame). A --record-trace recording of a session that played a scope cannot itself be played in-game from a frame inside or after that scope: a recorder writes no playback_answers or resume_bridge (only an instant-replay journal does), so its scene's playback requests and its resumption after the scope are not known (it replays exactly with --replay-trace, which runs the scope again). Rumble in joystick mode asks the devices door for the joysticks (glitchygames/input/rumble.py); inside a scope each send still asks the scope's door, with a device cache of its own, and then sends to no device (rule 8), so the played recording's answers are taken as it gave them. The scope's rumble controller starts fresh, though: a rumble the live game sent before the played scene began, still running when it was recorded, is not known to it, so its sends (and the counts they ask) can fall on other frames than the recording's; that matters only when the played recording's joystick count changed part way.

class PlaybackRequest(BaseModel):
    """A playback scope to enter at the start of the next frame (read-only; rule 1).

    Attributes:
        sources: The scoped doors the playback runs on.
        start: The start of the scene to rebuild (the ``scene_start`` the first played frame
            holds).
        scene_class: The class ``start.scene_class`` names.
        then: The scene to make active when the scope ends.
        kind: What the scope plays.
        frame_count: How many recorded frames the scope plays at most (from its first played
            frame to the recording's end); the ``playback`` control event's ``frames``.
        first_logic_frame: ``start.first_logic_frame``: the state the first played frame
            began in (glitchygames/scene_start.py, rule 7).

    """

    # Live objects (doors, scenes) are held as they are, never copied or validated deeply
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra='forbid', arbitrary_types_allowed=True)

    sources: PlaybackSources
    start: SceneStart
    scene_class: type[Scene]
    then: Scene
    kind: PlaybackKind
    frame_count: int
    first_logic_frame: FirstLogicFrame

    def begin_session(
        self: Self, *, live_scene: Scene, previous_scene: Scene | None, fps_event_seconds: float
    ) -> PlaybackSession:
        """Save what the scope's end restores, as the scope begins (rule 2).

        Args:
            live_scene: The active scene, stashed for the scope.
            previous_scene: ``SceneManager.previous_scene``, which the playback's own scene
                switches change.
            fps_event_seconds: When the live game last posted an FPS event.

        Returns:
            The session, holding the random streams and frame clock as they are now.

        """
        return PlaybackSession(
            sources=self.sources,
            live_scene=live_scene,
            saved_previous_scene=previous_scene,
            then=self.then,
            kind=self.kind,
            saved_random_states=capture_stream_states(),
            saved_frame_clock_seconds=frame_clock_seconds(),
            saved_fps_event_seconds=fps_event_seconds,
        )

        saved_fps_event_seconds: When the live game last posted an FPS event
            (``SceneManager._previous_fps_event_seconds``), on the live frame clock.

    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra='forbid', arbitrary_types_allowed=True)

    sources: PlaybackSources
    live_scene: Scene
    saved_previous_scene: Scene | None
    then: Scene
    kind: PlaybackKind
    saved_random_states: dict[str, Any]
    saved_frame_clock_seconds: float
    saved_fps_event_seconds: float

PlaybackSources #

A playback scope's doors (implements glitchygames.sources.EngineSources; rule 5).

Attributes:
  • base –

    The installed doors underneath (live, recording or a replay of the session).

  • replay –

    The replay serving the recording to the playback's scene.

  • exit_on_input –

    True when any key or button press ends the scope.

  • fast_forward_frames –

    How many of the scope's first frames run unpresented, unpaced and silent (rule 6).

  • is_fast_forwarding –

    True while the frame running (or about to run) is one of them: fewer frames compared than fast_forward_frames.

  • exit_requested –

    True once such a press arrived.

  • recording_quit –

    True once the recording asked to quit (its window's QUIT, or the playback scene's own quit_game()): the scope ends, the game does not quit.

  • captures_scene_starts –

    True: scenes built inside the scope capture their starts.

  • random_seed –

    The recording's master seed.

  • frames_played –

    How many frames the replay compared so far.

  • end_reason (PlaybackEndReason | None) –

    Why the scope should end now, or None while it plays on: the first found of the player's exit press ('exit_input') and the recording's quit ('recording_quit'), found by the frame's pumps, the game's request ('ended_by_game', set by SceneManager.end_playback), then the replay's end ('end_of_recording', 'truncated' or 'diverged'), found by compare_frame.

  • last_base_snapshot (InputSnapshot) –

    The installed doors' latest polled input (the live input as the scope began, then each frame's): the live game's input when the scope ends.

  • held_live_events (list[RedeliveredEvent]) –

    The live game's events the scope's pumps drained and held, each with its origin, in pump order: its own posts made before the scope (internal) and the player's releases, device and window events (external, PLAYBACK_HELD_EVENT_TYPES; the live game's input posts of those types among them). Delivered before the first pump after the scope.

  • input_posts_at_pump (list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]]) –

    The pending posts that were input posts (recording.post_input_event) as the current pump began, noted before the installed doors pump: a replay's pump (a session replayed) forgets the tracker's posts, their input marks included, once it has sorted its batch.

  • held_live_game_posts (list[tuple[Event, bool]]) –

    The posts the live game's own supervisors and handlers made during the scope (recording.live_game_posts) that the scope's pumps drained, in pump order, each with whether it was an input post (recording.post_input_event; only of a type SDL never generates: an SDL type's is the player's input, rule 5). Posted again as the scope ends, as they were posted (SceneManager._exit_playback).

  • live_posts_before_scope (list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]]) –

    The live game's posts no pump had returned yet as the scope began (its first pump holds them; rule 5).

  • has_pumped –

    True once the scope's doors pumped: from then on every post still pending is the scope's own (SceneManager._exit_playback drops those as it ends), but for the live game's supervisors' and handlers' (recording.live_game_posts, posted again as it ends).

  • installed_frame_seconds (float | None) –

    The installed doors' answer to the last frame_seconds call (the live measurement, or the session's recorded dt when it is replayed), or None before the first: the frame time the installed doors' end_frame gets (rule 5), not the played recording's that the frame runs with.
