class PlaybackSources:
    """A playback scope's doors (implements glitchygames.sources.EngineSources; rule 5).

    Attributes:
        base: The installed doors underneath (live, recording or a replay of the session).
        replay: The replay serving the recording to the playback's scene.
        exit_on_input: True when any key or button press ends the scope.
        fast_forward_frames: How many of the scope's first frames run unpresented, unpaced and
            silent (rule 6).
        is_fast_forwarding: True while the frame running (or about to run) is one of them:
            fewer frames compared than ``fast_forward_frames``.
        exit_requested: True once such a press arrived.
        recording_quit: True once the recording asked to quit (its window's QUIT, or the
            playback scene's own ``quit_game()``): the scope ends, the game does not quit.
        captures_scene_starts: True: scenes built inside the scope capture their starts.
        random_seed: The recording's master seed.
        frames_played: How many frames the replay compared so far.
        end_reason: Why the scope should end now, or None while it plays on: the first found
            of the player's exit press (``'exit_input'``) and the recording's quit
            (``'recording_quit'``), found by the frame's pumps, the game's request
            (``'ended_by_game'``, set by ``SceneManager.end_playback``), then the replay's end
            (``'end_of_recording'``, ``'truncated'`` or ``'diverged'``), found by
            ``compare_frame``.
        last_base_snapshot: The installed doors' latest polled input (the live input as the
            scope began, then each frame's): the live game's input when the scope ends.
        held_live_events: The live game's events the scope's pumps drained and held, each
            with its origin, in pump order: its own posts made before the scope (internal) and
            the player's releases, device and window events (external,
            ``PLAYBACK_HELD_EVENT_TYPES``; the live game's input posts of those types among
            them). Delivered before the first pump after the scope.
        input_posts_at_pump: The pending posts that were input posts
            (``recording.post_input_event``) as the current pump began, noted before the
            installed doors pump: a replay's pump (a session replayed) forgets the tracker's
            posts, their input marks included, once it has sorted its batch.
        held_live_game_posts: The posts the live game's own supervisors and handlers made
            during the scope (``recording.live_game_posts``) that the scope's pumps drained, in
            pump order, each with whether it was an input post (``recording.post_input_event``;
            only of a type SDL never generates: an SDL type's is the player's input, rule 5).
            Posted again as the scope ends, as they were posted (``SceneManager._exit_playback``).
        live_posts_before_scope: The live game's posts no pump had returned yet as the scope
            began (its first pump holds them; rule 5).
        has_pumped: True once the scope's doors pumped: from then on every post still pending
            is the scope's own (``SceneManager._exit_playback`` drops those as it ends), but
            for the live game's supervisors' and handlers' (``recording.live_game_posts``,
            posted again as it ends).
        installed_frame_seconds: The installed doors' answer to the last ``frame_seconds``
            call (the live measurement, or the session's recorded dt when it is replayed), or
            None before the first: the frame time the installed doors' ``end_frame`` gets
            (rule 5), not the played recording's that the frame runs with.

    """

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        *,
        base: EngineSources,
        replay: ReplaySources,
        exit_on_input: bool,
        fast_forward_frames: int = 0,
    ) -> None:
        """Wrap the installed doors and a replay.

        Args:
            base: The installed doors.
            replay: The replay sources (``playback_replay_sources``).
            exit_on_input: True to end the scope at any key or button press.
            fast_forward_frames: How many of the scope's first frames to fast-forward (rule 6).

        """
        self.base = base
        self.replay = replay
        self.exit_on_input = exit_on_input
        self.fast_forward_frames = fast_forward_frames
        # A plain attribute, kept by compare_frame (the class has as many methods as it may)
        self.is_fast_forwarding = fast_forward_frames > 0
        # Keeps the fast-forwarded frames silent (the rebuild's code path); the live game's
        # sounds playing as the scope began play on
        self._silencer = FrameSilencer(spares_playing_sounds=True)
        self.exit_requested = False
        self.recording_quit = False
        # The EngineSources property, as a plain attribute: set once, for the whole scope
        self.captures_scene_starts = True
        self.random_seed = replay.random_seed
        self.frames_played = 0
        self.end_reason: PlaybackEndReason | None = None
        self.last_base_snapshot: InputSnapshot = current_input()
        self.held_live_events: list[RedeliveredEvent] = []
        self.held_live_game_posts: list[tuple[pygame.event.Event, bool]] = []
        self.input_posts_at_pump: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]] = []
        self.live_posts_before_scope: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]] = []
        self.has_pumped = False
        self.installed_frame_seconds: float | None = None

    def _note_end(self: Self, *, reason: PlaybackEndReason) -> None:
        """Keep why the scope should end; the first reason found wins (``end_reason``)."""
        if self.end_reason is None:
            self.end_reason = reason

    @property
    def opened_save_namespaces(self: Self) -> Mapping[str, SaveManager]:
        """The replay's sandboxed save stores, by namespace."""
        return self.replay.opened_save_namespaces

    @property
    def stop_requested(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Whether the installed doors want the run to end (the scope never stops it)."""
        return self.base.stop_requested

    @property
    def presents_frames(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Whether the frame is presented: never while fast-forwarding, else as the doors do."""
        return not self.is_fast_forwarding and self.base.presents_frames

    @property
    def draws_overlay(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Whether the installed doors draw an overlay of their own."""
        return self.base.draws_overlay

    def on_installed(self: Self) -> None:
        """Note the live game's pending posts and input, then let the replay own the tracker.

        A scope that fast-forwards follows the game's music controls from here (rule 6), so
        the rebuilt scene's own are followed too.
        """
        self.live_posts_before_scope = list(pending_internal_posts())
        self.has_pumped = False
        self.last_base_snapshot = current_input()
        if self.is_fast_forwarding:
            self._silencer.begin()
        self.replay.on_installed()

    def on_uninstalled(self: Self) -> None:
        """Let the replay give up the post tracker; end a fast-forward's silence (rule 6)."""
        self._silencer.finish()
        self.replay.on_uninstalled()

    def pump_events(self: Self) -> list[pygame.event.Event]:
        """Pump the installed doors once; serve the replay's batch plus the window's QUIT (rule 5).

        Returns:
            The replay's batch in its recorded order without any QUIT (the recording's quit
            ends the scope instead), then any QUIT the installed doors read.

        """
        pending = pending_internal_posts()
        posted_before_pump = list(pending)
        self.input_posts_at_pump = [post for post in posted_before_pump if is_input_post(post=post)]
        base_events = self.base.pump_events()
        # The posts the live game made before the scope come first (pending is in posting
        # order, and nothing pumped between the scope's start and its first pump)
        is_first_pump = not self.has_pumped
        self.has_pumped = True
        live_post_count = len(self.live_posts_before_scope) if is_first_pump else 0
        posts_since_scope = posted_before_pump[live_post_count:]
        # The live game's own supervisors and handlers posted some since: theirs, not the scope's
        live_game_posts_since_scope = [
            post for post in posts_since_scope if is_live_game_post(post=post)
        ]
        scope_posts = [post for post in posts_since_scope if not is_live_game_post(post=post)]
        # This pump returns every one of them (or none ever will): sorted out from here on
        live_game_posts().clear()
        internal_events, quit_events = self._sort_base_events(
            base_events=base_events,
            live_posts=posted_before_pump[:live_post_count],
            live_game_posts=live_game_posts_since_scope,
            scope_posts=list(scope_posts),
            is_first_pump=is_first_pump,
        )
        # The installed doors' recorder (if any) consumed the posts it matched; the replay
        # classifies the internal events again, from the scope's posts alone
        pending[:] = scope_posts
        replay_batch: list[pygame.event.Event] = []
        for event in self.replay.pump_events(real_events=internal_events):
            if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
                self.recording_quit = True
                self._note_end(reason='recording_quit')
            else:
                replay_batch.append(event)
        return [*replay_batch, *quit_events]

    def _sort_base_events(
        self: Self,
        *,
        base_events: list[pygame.event.Event],
        live_posts: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]],
        live_game_posts: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]],
        scope_posts: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]],
        is_first_pump: bool,
    ) -> tuple[list[pygame.event.Event], list[pygame.event.Event]]:
        """Sort the installed doors' batch for the replay, the game and the exit check (rule 5).

        Holds the live game's posts and the events it must not lose (``held_live_events``,
        ``held_live_game_posts``).

        Args:
            base_events: The installed doors' batch.
            live_posts: Posts the live game made before the scope (matches are removed).
            live_game_posts: Posts the live game's own supervisors and handlers made during
                the scope (``recording.live_game_posts``; matches are removed).
            scope_posts: Posts the scope's code made since it began (matches are removed).
            is_first_pump: True for the scope's first pump, whose untracked internal events
                were posted before the scope.

        Returns:
            The internal events for the replay, and the QUIT events for the game.

        """
        internal_events: list[pygame.event.Event] = []
        quit_events: list[pygame.event.Event] = []
        # A replay of the session knows each served event's recorded origin (None live)
        served_origins = replayed_batch_origins(doors=self.base)
        for index, event in enumerate(base_events):
            scope_post = (
                take_matching_post(event=event, pending=scope_posts)
                if event.type == pygame.QUIT
                else None
            )
            if event.type == pygame.QUIT and scope_post is None:
                # The player's (or the live game's own) quit request still quits the game
                self._take_live_post(
                    event=event, live_posts=live_posts, live_game_posts=live_game_posts
                )
                quit_events.append(event)
            elif event.type == pygame.QUIT:
                _add_scope_post(
                    event=event,
                    is_input=_is_one_of(post=scope_post, posts=self.input_posts_at_pump),
                    internal_events=internal_events,
                )
            elif self._sort_live_post(
                event=event,
                live_posts=live_posts,
                live_game_posts=live_game_posts,
            ):
                continue
            elif (scope_post := take_matching_post(event=event, pending=scope_posts)) is not None:
                _add_scope_post(
                    event=event,
                    is_input=_is_one_of(post=scope_post, posts=self.input_posts_at_pump),
                    internal_events=internal_events,
                )
            elif served_origins is not None and _is_served_live_input_post(
                event=event, origin=served_origins[index]
            ):
                # The live game's input post the replay serves without its poster: held as
                # the live run held it (_sort_live_post)
                if is_first_pump:
                    self.held_live_events.append((event, EXTERNAL_ORIGIN))
                else:
                    self.held_live_game_posts.append((event, True))
            elif event_origin(event=event, pending=[]) == INTERNAL_ORIGIN:
                # Internal by type alone: on the first pump, posted before the scope began
                if is_first_pump:
                    self.held_live_events.append((event, INTERNAL_ORIGIN))
                else:
                    internal_events.append(event)
            else:
                self._sort_player_event(event=event)
        return internal_events, quit_events

    def _sort_player_event(self: Self, *, event: pygame.event.Event) -> None:
        """Sort the player's input (``_sort_base_events``): held, an exit press, or dropped.

        Releases, device and window events are held for the live game
        (``PLAYBACK_HELD_EVENT_TYPES``); a press ends a scope that exits on input
        (``PLAYBACK_EXIT_EVENT_TYPES``); anything else (a press without exit on input, motion)
        reaches nothing. A live input post of an SDL type is sorted here too (rule 5).

        Args:
            event: The external event.

        """
        if event.type in PLAYBACK_HELD_EVENT_TYPES:
            self.held_live_events.append((event, EXTERNAL_ORIGIN))
        elif self.exit_on_input and event.type in PLAYBACK_EXIT_EVENT_TYPES:
            self.exit_requested = True
            self._note_end(reason='exit_input')

    @staticmethod
    def _take_live_post(
        *,
        event: pygame.event.Event,
        live_posts: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]],
        live_game_posts: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]],
    ) -> bool:
        """Remove the live game's post that ``event`` is, if it is one (``_sort_base_events``).

        Returns:
            True when it was a post the live game made before the scope or during it.

        """
        return take_internal_post(event=event, pending=live_posts) or take_internal_post(
            event=event, pending=live_game_posts
        )

    def _sort_live_post(
        self: Self,
        *,
        event: pygame.event.Event,
        live_posts: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]],
        live_game_posts: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]],
    ) -> bool:
        """Sort ``event`` if it is one of the live game's posts (``_sort_base_events``, rule 5).

        An input post (``recording.post_input_event``) of an SDL type stands in for the player
        (BUGS.md #196): it is sorted as the player's input (``_sort_player_event``), so a press
        ends a demo, as it does in a replay of the session, which serves it from the recording
        without the poster. Any other post is held: one made before the scope joins
        ``held_live_events`` (redelivered as the scope ends; an input post of a type SDL never
        generates as external, as recorded); one the live game's supervisors and handlers made
        during it joins ``held_live_game_posts`` (posted again as the scope ends).

        Returns:
            True when it was one of the live game's posts (sorted or held).

        """
        live_post = take_matching_post(event=event, pending=live_posts)
        live_game_post = (
            None
            if live_post is not None
            else take_matching_post(event=event, pending=live_game_posts)
        )
        if live_post is None and live_game_post is None:
            return False
        matched_post = live_post if live_post is not None else live_game_post
        is_input = _is_one_of(post=matched_post, posts=self.input_posts_at_pump)
        if is_input and _is_sdl_event_type(event_type=event.type):
            self._sort_player_event(event=event)
        elif live_post is not None:
            self.held_live_events.append((event, EXTERNAL_ORIGIN if is_input else INTERNAL_ORIGIN))
        else:
            self.held_live_game_posts.append((event, is_input))
        return True

    def frame_seconds(self: Self, *, measured: float) -> float:
        """Return the recording's dt, after asking the installed doors as always.

        The installed doors' answer is kept (``installed_frame_seconds``) for their
        ``end_frame``.

        Returns:
            Seconds (past the recording's end, the installed doors' answer).

        """
        self.installed_frame_seconds = self.base.frame_seconds(measured=measured)
        return self.replay.frame_seconds(measured=self.installed_frame_seconds)

    def performance_frame_seconds(self: Self, *, measured: float, frame_seconds: float) -> float:
        """Return the installed doors' frame time for FPS events and the statistics.

        Returns:
            Seconds.

        """
        return self.base.performance_frame_seconds(measured=measured, frame_seconds=frame_seconds)

    def paced_frame_seconds(self: Self) -> float | None:
        """Return how the frame is paced: not at all while fast-forwarding (rule 6).

        Otherwise as the installed doors pace it (a demo plays at the game's speed).

        Returns:
            Seconds (0.0: unpaced), or None for the target FPS.

        """
        if self.is_fast_forwarding:
            return 0.0
        return self.base.paced_frame_seconds()

    def hold_frame(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Return whether the installed doors hold the frame.

        Returns:
            True to run no frame now.

        """
        return self.base.hold_frame()

    def draw_overlay(self: Self, *, surface: pygame.Surface) -> None:
        """Let the installed doors draw their overlay."""
        self.base.draw_overlay(surface=surface)

    def input_snapshot(self: Self) -> InputSnapshot:
        """Read the installed doors' snapshot (a recording keeps it), then serve the replay's.

        Returns:
            The recording's polled input for this frame.

        """
        self.last_base_snapshot = self.base.input_snapshot()
        return self.replay.input_snapshot()

    def devices(self: Self) -> DeviceRegistry:
        """Return the replay's registry of recorded devices.

        Returns:
            The registry.

        """
        return self.replay.devices()

    def saves(self: Self, *, namespace: str) -> SaveManager:
        """Return the replay's sandboxed store for ``namespace``.

        Returns:
            A memory store: real saves are never touched.

        """
        return self.replay.saves(namespace=namespace)

    def wall_clock_time(self: Self) -> datetime:
        """Return the recording's wall clock.

        Returns:
            Timezone-aware UTC time.

        """
        return self.replay.wall_clock_time()

    def control_events_for_frame(self: Self, *, frame_number: int) -> list[ControlEvent]:
        """Return the installed doors' control events to apply again on this frame (rule 5).

        The session's (a replay of the session re-applies a breakpoint on a frame the scope
        played, so a bookmark there pauses), never the played recording's: a breakpoint an
        instant-replay journal kept was the live session's, applied then, and is not applied
        again inside its playback.

        Returns:
            The control events.

        """
        return self.base.control_events_for_frame(frame_number=frame_number)

    def end_frame(
        self: Self,
        *,
        frame_number: int,
        dt: float,
        scene: Scene | None,
        control_events: list[ControlEvent],
        processing_seconds: float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Compare the frame with the recording, then let the installed doors end it (rule 5).

        The scene manager calls the two halves itself (``compare_frame``, then the installed
        doors' ``end_frame``), so only the comparison's errors end the scope; this is the
        EngineSources door for any other caller. The installed doors end the frame even when
        the comparison raises.
        """
        try:
            self.compare_frame(
                frame_number=frame_number, dt=dt, scene=scene, control_events=control_events
            )
        finally:
            self.base.end_frame(
                frame_number=frame_number,
                dt=dt,
                scene=scene,
                control_events=control_events,
                processing_seconds=processing_seconds,
            )

    def compare_frame(
        self: Self,
        *,
        frame_number: int,
        dt: float,
        scene: Scene | None,
        control_events: list[ControlEvent],
    ) -> None:
        """Compare the frame with the recording (the scope's half of ``end_frame``; rule 5).

        The scope's own ``playback`` marker is left out: it belongs to the session, not to the
        recording played. A fast-forwarded frame is silenced first (every sound it started
        stopped, music paused); after the last one, the silence ends (rule 6).
        """
        was_fast_forwarding = self.is_fast_forwarding
        if was_fast_forwarding:
            self._silencer.silence_frame()
        self.replay.end_frame(
            frame_number=frame_number,
            dt=dt,
            scene=scene,
            control_events=[
                control_event
                for control_event in control_events
                if control_event.kind != PLAYBACK_KIND
            ],
        )
        self.frames_played += 1
        self.is_fast_forwarding = self.frames_played < self.fast_forward_frames
        if was_fast_forwarding and not self.is_fast_forwarding:
            # The shown frames play their sounds, and the music plays on
            self._silencer.finish()
        if self.replay.stop_requested:
            replay_end_reason = self.replay.result.end_reason
            if replay_end_reason == 'diverged':
                self._note_end(reason='diverged')
            elif replay_end_reason == 'truncated':
                self._note_end(reason='truncated')
            else:
                self._note_end(reason='end_of_recording')

def compare_frame(
    self: Self,
    *,
    frame_number: int,
    dt: float,
    scene: Scene | None,
    control_events: list[ControlEvent],
) -> None:
    """Compare the frame with the recording (the scope's half of ``end_frame``; rule 5).

    The scope's own ``playback`` marker is left out: it belongs to the session, not to the
    recording played. A fast-forwarded frame is silenced first (every sound it started
    stopped, music paused); after the last one, the silence ends (rule 6).
    """
    was_fast_forwarding = self.is_fast_forwarding
    if was_fast_forwarding:
        self._silencer.silence_frame()
    self.replay.end_frame(
        frame_number=frame_number,
        dt=dt,
        scene=scene,
        control_events=[
            control_event
            for control_event in control_events
            if control_event.kind != PLAYBACK_KIND
        ],
    )
    self.frames_played += 1
    self.is_fast_forwarding = self.frames_played < self.fast_forward_frames
    if was_fast_forwarding and not self.is_fast_forwarding:
        # The shown frames play their sounds, and the music plays on
        self._silencer.finish()
    if self.replay.stop_requested:
        replay_end_reason = self.replay.result.end_reason
        if replay_end_reason == 'diverged':
            self._note_end(reason='diverged')
        elif replay_end_reason == 'truncated':
            self._note_end(reason='truncated')
        else:
            self._note_end(reason='end_of_recording')

def end_frame(
    self: Self,
    *,
    frame_number: int,
    dt: float,

    The scene manager calls the two halves itself (``compare_frame``, then the installed

    finally:
        self.base.end_frame(
            frame_number=frame_number,
            dt=dt,
            scene=scene,
            control_events=control_events,
            processing_seconds=processing_seconds,
        )

def pump_events(self: Self) -> list[pygame.event.Event]:
    """Pump the installed doors once; serve the replay's batch plus the window's QUIT (rule 5).

    Returns:
        The replay's batch in its recorded order without any QUIT (the recording's quit
        ends the scope instead), then any QUIT the installed doors read.

    """
    pending = pending_internal_posts()
    posted_before_pump = list(pending)
    self.input_posts_at_pump = [post for post in posted_before_pump if is_input_post(post=post)]
    base_events = self.base.pump_events()
    # The posts the live game made before the scope come first (pending is in posting
    # order, and nothing pumped between the scope's start and its first pump)
    is_first_pump = not self.has_pumped
    self.has_pumped = True
    live_post_count = len(self.live_posts_before_scope) if is_first_pump else 0
    posts_since_scope = posted_before_pump[live_post_count:]
    # The live game's own supervisors and handlers posted some since: theirs, not the scope's
    live_game_posts_since_scope = [
        post for post in posts_since_scope if is_live_game_post(post=post)
    ]
    scope_posts = [post for post in posts_since_scope if not is_live_game_post(post=post)]
    # This pump returns every one of them (or none ever will): sorted out from here on
    live_game_posts().clear()
    internal_events, quit_events = self._sort_base_events(
        base_events=base_events,
        live_posts=posted_before_pump[:live_post_count],
        live_game_posts=live_game_posts_since_scope,
        scope_posts=list(scope_posts),
        is_first_pump=is_first_pump,
    )
    # The installed doors' recorder (if any) consumed the posts it matched; the replay
    # classifies the internal events again, from the scope's posts alone
    pending[:] = scope_posts
    replay_batch: list[pygame.event.Event] = []
    for event in self.replay.pump_events(real_events=internal_events):
        if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
            self.recording_quit = True
            self._note_end(reason='recording_quit')
        else:
            replay_batch.append(event)
    return [*replay_batch, *quit_events]

    The scene's code gets the same answers when its instant-replay journal is played back

    return granted

def fast_forward_frame_count(
    *, frames: Sequence[dict[str, Any]], start_frame: int, shown_seconds: float
) -> int:
    """Return how many frames an instant replay fast-forwards before the seconds it shows.

    A frame is shown when the frame time from its start to the recording's end (its ``dt``
    and every later frame's, summed exactly, then rounded once to a float) is at most
    ``shown_seconds``; every earlier frame from ``start_frame`` is fast-forwarded (rule 7).
    So ten frames of ``dt`` d are shown for ``shown_seconds`` 10 * d, whatever float rounding
    a running sum would add.

    Args:
        frames: The recording's decoded frames.
        start_frame: The frame the playback starts at.
        shown_seconds: The frame time to show (``Scene.INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS``).

    Returns:
        The number of frames, from ``start_frame``, to fast-forward.

    """
    first_shown_frame = len(frames)
    seconds_to_end = Fraction(0)
    for frame_index in range(len(frames) - 1, start_frame - 1, -1):
        seconds_to_end += Fraction(frames[frame_index][DT_FIELD])
        if float(seconds_to_end) > shown_seconds:
            break
        first_shown_frame = frame_index
    return first_shown_frame - start_frame

def find_scene_class(*, name: str, module: str | None = None) -> type[Scene] | None:
    """Return the loaded ``Scene`` subclass a start names (rule 1).

    Only loaded classes are searched: nothing is imported from recording data. The class
    defined in ``module`` with the qualified name ``name`` is taken when exactly one is
    loaded. Otherwise a class is taken by its qualified name alone only where the modules
    cannot be compared, as ``check_recorded_game`` decides for a recording's game: no module
    recorded, or a game run as a script (``__main__``) on either side; then the one such class
    is taken and several are refused. A class of that name from another module is another
    game's scene: refused.

    Args:
        name: A class's qualified name (``SceneStart.scene_class``).
        module: The module it is defined in (``SceneStart.scene_module``), or None.

    Returns:
        The class, or None when no loaded subclass matches or several match by name alone
        (logged).

    """
    named_alike: list[type[Scene]] = []
    seen: set[type[Scene]] = set()
    unvisited: collections.deque[type[Scene]] = collections.deque([Scene])
    while unvisited:
        scene_class = unvisited.popleft()
        for subclass in scene_class.__subclasses__():
            if subclass not in seen:
                seen.add(subclass)
                unvisited.append(subclass)
                if subclass.__qualname__ == name:
                    named_alike.append(subclass)
    exact_matches = [scene_class for scene_class in named_alike if scene_class.__module__ == module]
    if len(exact_matches) == 1:
        return exact_matches[0]
    matches_by_name = [
        scene_class
        for scene_class in named_alike
        if module is None or SCRIPT_MODULE_NAME in {module, scene_class.__module__}
    ]
    if len(matches_by_name) > 1:
        LOG.warning('Several scene classes are named %s; which to rebuild is unknown', name)
        return None
    return matches_by_name[0] if matches_by_name else None

processing #

Compare a replay's processing time with its recording's, frame by frame.

A recording made through the engine (--record-trace, --rebaseline, the scripted sessions) holds each frame's processing time (processing_seconds, a newest-first history across rebaselines: glitchygames/recording_history.py; this module compares [0]): the frame's work (logic, events, frame services, positioning and rendering), without presenting it, without the doors' own end_frame (writing the recording, comparing the replay) and without the pacing sleep. It is a diagnostic field: a replay never compares it and never serves it to the game (it is measured with clock.measured_seconds). The header's latest measurement run (measurement_runs[0]) names the machine that measured them (machine_description, never the host name).

--replay-trace PATH --headless --compare-processing measures this machine's processing time for every replayed frame the same way and reports how the two compare (ProcessingSummary.describe), after the replay's own report. --max-processing-slowdown PERCENT (which implies --compare-processing) turns it into a check: a replay that matched but whose total processing time exceeds the recording's by more than PERCENT exits ExitCode.PROCESSING_SLOWER; a recording with no processing times cannot be checked (ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT). Live runs are paced and headless replays are not, so totals of wall-clock time would not compare; processing times do. They only compare on the same machine (CI against a baseline recorded on its hardware): the report says when the machines differ.

Pacing changes processing time too: between paced frames the processor idles and slows down, so a live recording's frames take longer than the same work in an unpaced replay (a 330-frame Clockwork Keep session measured about 65% faster replayed than recorded live, on one machine). The latest measurement run says whether it paced its frames as recording began (processing_paced: a live run with a target FPS, True; a --rebaseline, a headless replay, False). The fair baseline is a --rebaseline of the session made on the machine that checks it: its times are measured unpaced, as a replay's are (the same session then compares within about 1%). Comparing against a paced recording, the report says so.

class ProcessingComparison:
    """Collects each replayed frame's processing time beside the recorded one."""

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        *,
        recorded_machine: str | None,
        replay_machine: str,
        recorded_paced: bool | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Start with no frames.

        Args:
            recorded_machine: The machine the recording's latest run names
                (``measurement_runs[0]``).
            replay_machine: This machine (``machine_description``).
            recorded_paced: Whether the recording's latest run paced its frames, or None when
                it does not say.

        """
        self._recorded_machine = recorded_machine
        self._replay_machine = replay_machine
        self._recorded_paced = recorded_paced
        # (frame index, recorded seconds, replayed seconds) of each compared frame
        self._frames: list[tuple[int, float, float]] = []
        self._frames_without_recorded_time = 0

    def add_frame(
        self: Self, *, frame_index: int, recorded_seconds: float | None, replayed_seconds: float
    ) -> None:
        """Add a replayed frame.

        Args:
            frame_index: The recording's frame index.
            recorded_seconds: Its recorded processing time, or None when the recording has none.
            replayed_seconds: Its processing time in this replay.

        """
        if recorded_seconds is None:
            self._frames_without_recorded_time += 1
            return
        self._frames.append((frame_index, recorded_seconds, replayed_seconds))

    def summary(self: Self) -> ProcessingSummary:
        """Return how the frames added so far compare.

        Returns:
            The summary.

        """
        recorded = [recorded_seconds for _frame, recorded_seconds, _replayed in self._frames]
        replayed = [replayed_seconds for _frame, _recorded, replayed_seconds in self._frames]
        grown = sorted(
            (
                SlowerFrame(frame=frame, extra_seconds=replayed_seconds - recorded_seconds)
                for frame, recorded_seconds, replayed_seconds in self._frames
                if replayed_seconds > recorded_seconds
            ),
            key=lambda slower_frame: slower_frame.extra_seconds,
            reverse=True,
        )
        return ProcessingSummary(
            frames_compared=len(self._frames),
            frames_without_recorded_time=self._frames_without_recorded_time,
            recorded_total_seconds=sum(recorded),
            replayed_total_seconds=sum(replayed),
            recorded_median_seconds=statistics.median(recorded) if recorded else None,
            replayed_median_seconds=statistics.median(replayed) if replayed else None,
            slowest_frames=tuple(grown[:SLOWEST_FRAME_COUNT]),
            recorded_machine=self._recorded_machine,
            replay_machine=self._replay_machine,
            recorded_paced=self._recorded_paced,
        )

class ProcessingSummary(BaseModel):
    """How a replay's processing time compared with its recording's.

    Attributes:
        frames_compared: Frames with both a recorded and a replayed time.
        frames_without_recorded_time: Replayed frames whose recording held no time.
        recorded_total_seconds: The compared frames' recorded processing time.
        replayed_total_seconds: The compared frames' processing time in this replay.
        recorded_median_seconds: The median recorded frame (None when nothing was compared).
        replayed_median_seconds: The median replayed frame (None when nothing was compared).
        slowest_frames: The frames that grew most, most first (only frames that grew).
        recorded_machine: The machine the recording's latest run names, or None.
        replay_machine: This machine.
        recorded_paced: Whether the recording's latest run paced its frames
            (``measurement_runs[0]``), or None when it does not say.

    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra='forbid')

    frames_compared: int
    frames_without_recorded_time: int
    recorded_total_seconds: float
    replayed_total_seconds: float
    recorded_median_seconds: float | None
    replayed_median_seconds: float | None
    slowest_frames: tuple[SlowerFrame, ...]
    recorded_machine: str | None
    replay_machine: str
    recorded_paced: bool | None

    @property
    def change_percent(self: Self) -> float | None:
        """How much longer (positive) or shorter (negative) the replay took, in percent.

        None when nothing was compared, or the recorded total is zero.
        """
        if self.frames_compared == 0 or self.recorded_total_seconds <= 0.0:
            return None
        return (self.replayed_total_seconds / self.recorded_total_seconds - 1.0) * PERCENT

    def exceeds(self: Self, *, max_slowdown_percent: float) -> bool:
        """Report whether the replay took more than ``max_slowdown_percent`` longer.

        Args:
            max_slowdown_percent: The allowed slowdown, in percent.

        Returns:
            True when it did; False when it did not, or nothing was compared.

        """
        change_percent = self.change_percent
        return change_percent is not None and change_percent > max_slowdown_percent

    def describe(self: Self) -> str:
        """Describe the comparison on one line (printed after the replay's report).

        Returns:
            ``Processing: the replay took 14.2% longer than the recording (...)``, or why
            nothing was compared.

        """
        change_percent = self.change_percent
        if change_percent is None:
            return (
                'Processing: nothing to compare: the recording holds no processing times '
                f'({self.frames_without_recorded_time} frames replayed)'
            )
        if change_percent > 0:
            change = f'{change_percent:.1f}% longer than'
        elif change_percent < 0:
            change = f'{-change_percent:.1f}% less time than'
        else:
            change = 'the same time as'
        # Frames were compared (change_percent is not None), so both medians exist
        replayed_median_seconds = self.replayed_median_seconds
        recorded_median_seconds = self.recorded_median_seconds
        assert replayed_median_seconds is not None
        assert recorded_median_seconds is not None
        totals = (
            f'Processing: the replay took {change} the recording ({self.frames_compared} '
            f'frames: {self.replayed_total_seconds:.3f} s against '
            f'{self.recorded_total_seconds:.3f} s; median frame '
            f'{_milliseconds(replayed_median_seconds)} against '
            f'{_milliseconds(recorded_median_seconds)})'
        )
        parts = [totals]
        if self.slowest_frames:
            slowest = ', '.join(
                f'frame {frame.frame} +{frame.extra_seconds * MILLISECONDS_PER_SECOND:.3f} ms'
                for frame in self.slowest_frames
            )
            parts.append(f'slowest against the recording: {slowest}')
        if self.frames_without_recorded_time:
            count = self.frames_without_recorded_time
            parts.append(f'{count} frame{"" if count == 1 else "s"} had no recorded time')
        if self.recorded_machine is None:
            parts.append('the recording does not name its machine')
        elif self.recorded_machine != self.replay_machine:
            parts.append(
                f'recorded on {self.recorded_machine}, replayed on {self.replay_machine}: '
                'times from different machines do not compare'
            )
        if self.recorded_paced is True:
            parts.append(
                'the recording was measured in a paced run, which runs slower than an unpaced '
                'replay: compare against a --rebaseline of it made on this machine'
            )
        return '; '.join(parts)

rebaseline #

Rebaseline: --replay-trace OLD --rebaseline NEW --headless.

A rebaseline replays OLD's inputs on the current code and writes what that code did to a new recording, NEW, with a summary of what changed. It is how a recording used as a regression test (tests/fixtures/replays, glitchygames/testing/replays.py) follows an intentional change; replacing OLD with NEW stays a deliberate, reviewed step: NEW is never OLD (refused), and nothing replaces OLD.

The rules:

  1. Options: --rebaseline NEW needs --replay-trace OLD and --headless (a watched replay holds frames and takes the viewer's keys, so it is refused rather than made headless behind the user's back), and refuses NEW or NEW's partial file (rule 4) naming OLD's file, --record-trace (the rebaseline writes its own recording), --audit and --replay-digest (the audit's tools: a rebaseline is not audited) and --replay-fps real (FPS events from this machine's frame times would be recorded as the new baseline); each refusal exits ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED (rebaseline_refusal). An unusable OLD is refused as by any replay (ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT, ExitCode.MISSING_INPUT).
  2. Replay: OLD is replayed as usual (glitchygames/replay/driver.py, rule 17 there), but a divergence does not stop it (ReplayOptions.stop_on_divergence False): it runs to OLD's last frame, or until the game ends, noting every frame that differs and every sprite that differs in them. OLD's input the run never received is never carried elsewhere (that would invent an input sequence OLD does not have); it is counted instead: the external events of batches a frame did not pump (it pumped fewer times than recorded), and OLD's frames after the game ended.
  3. Recording: RecordingSources over the replay (replayed; glitchygames/recording.py) write NEW with OLD's inputs, as the replay's doors served them: the event batches (origins from the replay's merge, so code-posted events stay internal and replaying NEW delivers nothing twice), dt, input_changes, re-applied control events, and each frame's saves_opened, devices_opened and device_enumeration copied from OLD's frame; and the current code's sprites and markers. The header is OLD's (rebaseline_header). NEW's frames stack this run's content hash and processing time in front of OLD's histories, and its header this run's measurement_runs entry in front of OLD's (glitchygames/recording_history.py), so an unchanged game shows the same hash one entry deeper, and a changed one shows which frames changed.
  4. Writing: NEW is written to NEW.partial (glitchygames.output_files.partial_path) and moved into place once the run ended normally, so NEW is never left half written; a run that a crash, a signal or the game's own failing exit (sys.exit(1)) ended early writes nothing (the partial file is removed). The game's own successful exit (sys.exit(0), sys.exit()) is the game ending early, as quit_game() is: NEW holds the frames that ran (not the one it left part way through) and the run exits ExitCode.REBASELINE_INPUT_LOST (rule 5). A partial file that cannot be written is refused before the replay starts, on one line, with ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT (GameEngine._refuse_unwritable_outputs). If the final move fails, the finished partial file is kept, its path logged and printed, and the run exits ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT.
  5. Output: the summary (RebaselineSummary.describe) is printed to stdout instead of the replay's report, e.g. Rebaselined 9800 frames to NEW: 412 frames differ (first at 6120: sprite Ball#2 rect expected [412, 300, 16, 16], got [412, 301, 16, 16]); sprites affected: Ball#2, Ball#3 or Rebaselined 9800 frames to NEW: no frames differ, followed by the lost input (rule 2) when there is any, e.g. ; 3 recorded input events not delivered (first at frame 812); ended at frame 500 of 9800, which is also logged as a warning. The run exits ExitCode.SUCCESS (ReplayExitPolicy.SUCCESS_AFTER_WRITING) however many frames differ, but ExitCode.REBASELINE_INPUT_LOST when input was lost (ReplayResult.has_lost_input), so a script notices: NEW is still written (it replays clean), but it is not a faithful re-run of OLD's session.

NEW replays on the current code with no divergence, as long as the rebaseline replayed all of OLD: a truncated OLD gives a truncated NEW (source_truncated), whose replay matches to its cut-off and exits ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT, as any truncated recording does; and a run that ended before OLD's last frame (the lost input of rule 2) records only the frames it ran.

    NEW's file.

class Rebaseline:
    """Records a rebaseline's replay into the new recording and writes it (rules 3 to 5).

    ``GameEngine`` creates it for ``--rebaseline``, calls ``start_recording`` before the first
    frame and, once the run is over and the recorder closed, ``write`` (a normal end) or
    ``discard``.

    Attributes:
        destination: NEW's file.
        write_failed: True once ``write`` could not move the partial file into place (the
            engine then exits ``ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT``).

    """

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        *,
        replay_sources: ReplaySources,
        source_path: Path,
        destination: Path,
        measurement_run: MeasurementRun,
    ) -> None:
        """Keep what the rebaseline needs.

        Args:
            replay_sources: The replay of OLD (``ReplayOptions.stop_on_divergence`` False).
            source_path: OLD's file.
            destination: NEW's file.
            measurement_run: This run's provenance, put in front of OLD's runs in NEW's header
                (``GameEngine.measurement_run``).

        """
        self._replay_sources = replay_sources
        self._measurement_run = measurement_run
        self._source_path = source_path
        self.destination = destination
        self.write_failed = False
        self._partial_path = partial_path(destination=destination)

    def start_recording(self: Self) -> GameplayRecorder:
        """Open the partial file and install recording doors over the replay (rule 3).

        Returns:
            The recorder (the engine closes it at teardown).

        """
        header = rebaseline_header(
            original_header=self._replay_sources.header,
            original_path=self._source_path,
            measurement_run=self._measurement_run,
            original_frames=self._replay_sources.recording.frames,
            source_truncated=self._replay_sources.recording.is_truncated,
        )
        recorder = GameplayRecorder(path=self._partial_path, header=header)
        install_sources(
            sources=RecordingSources(
                inner=active_sources(), recorder=recorder, replayed=self._replay_sources
            )
        )
        LOG.info('Rebaselining %s to %s', self._source_path, self.destination)
        return recorder

    def write(self: Self, *, result: ReplayResult) -> str:
        """Move the closed recording into place and summarize the rebaseline (rules 4 and 5).

        Lost input (rule 2) is logged as a warning. A failed move keeps the partial file, logs
        it as an error and sets ``write_failed``.

        Args:
            result: The replay's settled result.

        Returns:
            The summary line, then (after a failed move) a line saying where the recording is.

        """
        summary = RebaselineSummary.from_result(result=result, path=self.destination)
        lost_input = summary.describe_lost_input()
        if lost_input is not None:
            LOG.warning('The rebaseline lost recorded input: %s', lost_input)
        move_error: OSError | None = None
        try:
            self._partial_path.replace(self.destination)
        except OSError as error:
            move_error = error
        if move_error is None:
            return summary.describe()
        self.write_failed = True
        # Logged without a traceback: the message says what failed and where the recording is
        LOG.error(
            'Could not move the rebaselined recording %s to %s (%s); it is kept at %s',
            self._partial_path,
            self.destination,
            move_error,
            self._partial_path,
        )
        return (
            f'{summary.describe()}\n{self._partial_path} could not be moved to '
            f'{self.destination} ({move_error}); the rebaselined recording is kept there'
        )

    def discard(self: Self) -> None:
        """Remove the partial recording of a run that ended early (rule 4)."""
        self._partial_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        LOG.warning('The rebaseline ended early; %s was not written', self.destination)

def start_recording(self: Self) -> GameplayRecorder:
    """Open the partial file and install recording doors over the replay (rule 3).

    Returns:
        The recorder (the engine closes it at teardown).

    header = rebaseline_header(

    )
    recorder = GameplayRecorder(path=self._partial_path, header=header)
    install_sources(
        sources=RecordingSources(
            inner=active_sources(), recorder=recorder, replayed=self._replay_sources
        )
    )
    LOG.info('Rebaselining %s to %s', self._source_path, self.destination)
    return recorder

def write(self: Self, *, result: ReplayResult) -> str:
    """Move the closed recording into place and summarize the rebaseline (rules 4 and 5).

    Lost input (rule 2) is logged as a warning. A failed move keeps the partial file, logs
    it as an error and sets ``write_failed``.

    Args:
        result: The replay's settled result.

    Returns:
        The summary line, then (after a failed move) a line saying where the recording is.

    """
    summary = RebaselineSummary.from_result(result=result, path=self.destination)
    lost_input = summary.describe_lost_input()
    if lost_input is not None:
        LOG.warning('The rebaseline lost recorded input: %s', lost_input)
    move_error: OSError | None = None
    try:
        self._partial_path.replace(self.destination)
    except OSError as error:
        move_error = error
    if move_error is None:
        return summary.describe()
    self.write_failed = True
    # Logged without a traceback: the message says what failed and where the recording is
    LOG.error(
        'Could not move the rebaselined recording %s to %s (%s); it is kept at %s',
        self._partial_path,
        self.destination,
        move_error,
        self._partial_path,
    )
    return (
        f'{summary.describe()}\n{self._partial_path} could not be moved to '
        f'{self.destination} ({move_error}); the rebaselined recording is kept there'
    )

class RebaselineSummary(BaseModel):
    """What changed between OLD and the current code (rule 5).

    Attributes:
        path: Where the new recording was written.
        first_divergence: The first difference (of any kind), or None when nothing differs.
        frames_differing: How many compared frames differed.
        sprites_affected: Every sprite that differed in them, in the order first found.
        frames_replayed: How many of OLD's frames were replayed (and written).
        frames_recorded: How many complete frames OLD holds.
        undelivered_input_count: OLD's external events in batches the run never pumped.
        first_undelivered_input_frame: The frame of the first of them, or None.

    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra='forbid')

    path: Path
    first_divergence: Divergence | None
    frames_differing: int
    sprites_affected: list[str]
    frames_replayed: int
    frames_recorded: int
    undelivered_input_count: int
    first_undelivered_input_frame: int | None

    @classmethod
    def from_result(cls, *, result: ReplayResult, path: Path) -> RebaselineSummary:
        """Summarize a rebaseline's replay result.

        Args:
            result: The replay's settled result (after ``ReplaySources.finish_run``).
            path: Where the new recording was written.

        Returns:
            The summary.

        """
        return cls(
            path=path,
            first_divergence=result.divergence,
            frames_differing=result.differing_frame_count,
            sprites_affected=list(result.affected_sprite_ids),
            frames_replayed=result.frames_replayed,
            frames_recorded=result.frames_recorded,
            undelivered_input_count=result.undelivered_input_count,
            first_undelivered_input_frame=result.first_undelivered_input_frame,
        )

    def describe_lost_input(self: Self) -> str | None:
        """Describe OLD's input the run never received (rule 2), if any.

        Returns:
            ``N recorded input events not delivered (first at frame F)`` and/or ``ended at
            frame R of T``, joined with ``; ``, or None when every recorded input was delivered.

        """
        parts: list[str] = []
        if self.undelivered_input_count > 0:
            events = (
                '1 recorded input event'
                if self.undelivered_input_count == 1
                else f'{self.undelivered_input_count} recorded input events'
            )
            parts.append(
                f'{events} not delivered (first at frame {self.first_undelivered_input_frame})'
            )
        if self.frames_replayed < self.frames_recorded:
            parts.append(f'ended at frame {self.frames_replayed} of {self.frames_recorded}')
        return '; '.join(parts) if parts else None

    def describe(self: Self) -> str:
        """Describe the rebaseline on one line (printed to stdout).

        Returns:
            ``Rebaselined N frames to NEW: `` then ``no frames differ``, ``K frames differ
            (first at F: <what differed>)`` with ``; sprites affected: A, B`` when sprites
            differed, or ``the run differs (at F: <what differed>)`` when no compared frame
            differed but the run did (it ended before OLD's last frame); then ``; `` and
            ``describe_lost_input()`` when input was lost.

        """
        line = f'Rebaselined {self.frames_replayed} frames to {self.path}: '
        line += self._describe_differences()
        lost_input = self.describe_lost_input()
        if lost_input is not None:
            line = f'{line}; {lost_input}'
        return line

    def _describe_differences(self: Self) -> str:
        divergence = self.first_divergence
        if divergence is None:
            return 'no frames differ'
        where = f'{divergence.frame_number}: {divergence.describe_difference()}'
        if self.frames_differing == 0:
            return f'the run differs (at {where})'
        count = (
            '1 frame differs'
            if self.frames_differing == 1
            else f'{self.frames_differing} frames differ'
        )
        differences = f'{count} (first at {where})'
        if self.sprites_affected:
            differences = f'{differences}; sprites affected: {", ".join(self.sprites_affected)}'
        return differences

def rebaseline_header(
    *,
    original_header: Mapping[str, Any],
    original_path: Path,
    measurement_run: MeasurementRun,
    original_frames: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None,
    source_truncated: bool = False,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the header of a recording rebaselined from another (rule 3).

    OLD's header is kept (the seed, start time, options, screen size, saves, devices and device
    enumeration answers: the replay ran with them, so NEW replays with them), with:
    ``rebaselined_from`` naming OLD, the engine, pygame and Python versions of this run (they
    produced NEW's sprites), this run's ``measurement_run`` in front of OLD's
    ``measurement_runs``, ``source_truncated`` when OLD was cut off (NEW then ends as
    truncated, as OLD's replay did), no ``input_capture_format_version`` (NEW records the
    polled input and markers the replay saw, as format 3) and no ``bookmarked_copy_of``: NEW
    is an original, never a bookmarked copy that S may rewrite in place (it may be moved over
    a golden fixture); it holds OLD's bookmark breakpoints, which a watched replay of NEW still
    loads as its bookmarks (glitchygames/replay/driver.py, rule 16).

    Args:
        original_header: OLD's header fields (without ``format_version`` and ``frames``).
        original_path: OLD's file.
        measurement_run: This run's provenance, put in front of OLD's ``measurement_runs``
            (its ``rebaselined_from`` is set to the header's, so both name OLD one way).
        original_frames: OLD's complete frames, decoded, or None: their count is OLD's newest
            run's ``frame_count``, and every earlier run without a ``summary`` gets one from
            them (``stacked_measurement_runs``).
        source_truncated: True when OLD was cut off part way.

    Returns:
        NEW's header fields.

    """
    header = dict(original_header)
    header.pop(INPUT_CAPTURE_FORMAT_HEADER_FIELD, None)
    header.pop(BOOKMARKED_COPY_OF_HEADER_FIELD, None)
    header[ENGINE_VERSION_HEADER_FIELD] = installed_engine_version()
    header[PYGAME_VERSION_HEADER_FIELD] = pygame.version.ver
    header[PYTHON_VERSION_HEADER_FIELD] = platform.python_version()
    # Each run's provenance, newest first; NEW's frames stack this run's histories the same way,
    # as glitchygames/recording_history.py describes
    for unreleased_field in UNRELEASED_HEADER_FIELDS:
        header.pop(unreleased_field, None)
    header[MEASUREMENT_RUNS_HEADER_FIELD] = stacked_measurement_runs(
        newest=measurement_run.model_copy(update={'rebaselined_from': str(original_path)}),
        previous=original_header.get(MEASUREMENT_RUNS_HEADER_FIELD),
        previous_frame_count=None if original_frames is None else len(original_frames),
        previous_frames=() if original_frames is None else original_frames,
        budget_seconds=budget_seconds_for(header=original_header),
    )
    header[REBASELINED_FROM_HEADER_FIELD] = str(original_path)
    if source_truncated:
        header[SOURCE_TRUNCATED_HEADER_FIELD] = True
    return header

def rebaseline_refusal(*, options: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    """Say why a rebaseline's options cannot run (rule 1), given ``--replay-trace``.

    Args:
        options: The parsed options (``rebaseline`` and ``replay_trace`` set).

    Returns:
        The reason, for the log, or None when the rebaseline can run.

    """
    if not options.get('headless'):
        return (
            '--rebaseline needs --headless: a watched replay holds frames and takes the '
            "viewer's keys"
        )
    path_refusal = _path_refusal(
        new_path=Path(options['rebaseline']), old_path=Path(options['replay_trace'])
    )
    if path_refusal is not None:
        return path_refusal
    # (the conflicting option is given, why it is refused), checked in order
    conflicting_options = (
        (
            options.get('record_trace') is not None,
            '--rebaseline writes its own recording, not with --record-trace',
        ),
        (bool(options.get('audit')), '--rebaseline replays once, not with --audit'),
        (
            options.get('replay_digest') is not None,
            '--rebaseline is not audited, not with --replay-digest',
        ),
        (
            options.get('replay_fps') == REAL_REPLAY_FPS,
            (
                '--rebaseline would record FPS events from measured frame times, not with '
                f'--replay-fps {REAL_REPLAY_FPS}'
            ),
        ),
    )
    return next((reason for is_given, reason in conflicting_options if is_given), None)

rebuild #

Step back in a watched replay: restart the replay process and rebuild up to a frame.

A replay cannot run backwards, and the engine cannot be rebuilt in-process (its scenes, sprites and singletons hold the state of every frame run so far). So , (step back), Home and D (glitchygames/replay/controls.py) restart the replay in a fresh process at a pause frame N:

  1. The watched replay ends its run with ReplayResult.restart_frame set (the result's end reason is 'restart', unless it already diverged or ended) and tears down as usual, which closes its window; the end-of-run performance and unhandled-event reports are skipped.
  2. GameEngine._restart_replay builds the restart's command (restart_command): this process's own command line (sys.orig_argv, so every option is kept, replay-local ones such as --replay-fps included) with --replay-trace (the recording) and --replay-pause-at-frame N replaced, an explicit --debug-overlay or --no-debug-overlay (whether the overlay was shown) and --replay-viewer-state (the speed, the debug overlay's panel and the divergence found so far, so D works at once: ViewerState). They are appended, the last occurrence of an option winning (an earlier abbreviation such as --debug-o included), before any bare --.
  3. relaunch_replay runs it, with the engine's signal handlers installed again (a SIGTERM or SIGHUP raises SystemExit, and subprocess.run then kills the child with SIGKILL, without its teardown, and reaps it: acceptable, as a replay never records). The first replay process becomes the supervisor: it runs each restarted replay as a child with glitchygames.process.run_command (the engine's one child-process launcher), adding --replay-restart-handoff PATH. A child that steps back again does not start a grandchild: it writes a RestartHandoff (its restart command and its own result's exit code) to that file, whole (written aside, then moved into place), and ends; the supervisor runs it next. So there are never more than two replay processes, however often the viewer steps back, and no process restarts itself. The supervisor exits with the last child's status, but a divergence in any earlier run is kept: when the last child ends with SUCCESS, the first non-success result handed over (or the first run's own) is the status. An unreadable handoff or a child that cannot start is logged and exits ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR.

The supervisor keeps the memory its own replay used (the engine's scenes, sprites, the recording's frames and pygame's modules: pygame is quit, the rest is not released) while the children run; only the first process supervises, so this is paid once, not per restart. 4. The restarted replay (ReplayOptions.pause_at_frame) skips the start screen (the viewer already started it) and rebuilds: frames 0 to N - 1 run in full but unpresented and unpaced, in silence (FrameSilencer, glitchygames/replay/silence.py, which an instant replay's fast-forward shares: Rebuild.silence_frame stops every sound a frame started after it, as Sound.play() gives its channel full volume again, and music is paused until the rebuild ends; Rebuild.begin follows the game's own music pauses, so music the game paused itself stays paused), presenting Rebuilding: frame k / N every REBUILD_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_SECONDS of real time and printing it every REBUILD_PROGRESS_PRINT_INTERVAL_SECONDS (Rebuild.progress_is_due), so the window does not look frozen. At frame N it pauses, showing frame N - 1's picture. Frame 0 always runs first (FIRST_PAUSED_FRAME), so a pause frame of 0 (Home) pauses after it. A game that asks the mixer what is playing may get a different answer during the rebuild than when it was recorded (glitchygames/replay/ silence.py says why the replay is unaffected).

os.execv would replace the process in place, but it is not used: starting a process without a shell is a security lint finding everywhere but the one authorised launcher (glitchygames.process.run_command).

class Rebuild(FrameSilencer):
    """A restarted replay's run up to its pause frame (module docstring, step 4).

    Its frames run in silence as an instant replay's fast-forward does: ``begin``,
    ``silence_frame``, ``stop_following_music`` and ``finish`` are ``FrameSilencer``'s
    (glitchygames/replay/silence.py).

    Attributes:
        target_frame: The frame the replay pauses at.

    """

    def __init__(self: Self, *, target_frame: int) -> None:
        """Prepare to rebuild up to ``target_frame``.

        Args:
            target_frame: The frame the replay pauses at (at least ``FIRST_PAUSED_FRAME``).

        """
        super().__init__()
        self.target_frame = target_frame
        # When the progress is next shown and printed (set by the first question)
        self._next_progress_seconds: float | None = None
        self._next_print_seconds: float | None = None

    def progress_is_due(self: Self, *, frame_index: int, now: float) -> bool:
        """Report whether the rebuild shows its progress before ``frame_index`` runs.

        Due every ``REBUILD_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_SECONDS`` of real time from the first question
        (which is never due); the progress line is printed to stdout at most every
        ``REBUILD_PROGRESS_PRINT_INTERVAL_SECONDS``, when a showing is due.

        Args:
            frame_index: The frame about to run.
            now: The measured time (``glitchygames.clock.measured_seconds``).

        Returns:
            True when the progress is to be shown now.

        """
        if self._next_progress_seconds is None or self._next_print_seconds is None:
            self._next_progress_seconds = now + REBUILD_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_SECONDS
            self._next_print_seconds = now + REBUILD_PROGRESS_PRINT_INTERVAL_SECONDS
            return False
        if now < self._next_progress_seconds:
            return False
        self._next_progress_seconds = max(
            self._next_progress_seconds + REBUILD_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_SECONDS, now
        )
        if now >= self._next_print_seconds:
            self._next_print_seconds = max(
                self._next_print_seconds + REBUILD_PROGRESS_PRINT_INTERVAL_SECONDS, now
            )
            progress_text = rebuild_progress_text(
                frame_index=frame_index, target_frame=self.target_frame
            )
            sys.stdout.write(f'{progress_text}\n')
            sys.stdout.flush()
        return True

def begin(self: Self) -> None:
    """Follow the game's music controls; note the sounds playing (``spares_playing_sounds``).

    Until ``finish`` (or ``stop_following_music``), the game's ``pause`` and ``unpause``
    calls are noted, so ``finish`` resumes music only when the game did not pause it
    itself. A game that bound the functions before (``from pygame.mixer.music import
    pause``) is not followed. Again: nothing.
    """
    if self._is_following_music:
        return
    self._is_following_music = True
    _MUSIC_FOLLOWING.add(silencer=self)
    if self.spares_playing_sounds and pygame.mixer.get_init() is not None:
        for channel_index in range(pygame.mixer.get_num_channels()):
            playing_sound = pygame.mixer.Channel(channel_index).get_sound()
            if playing_sound is not None:
                self._spared_sounds[channel_index] = playing_sound

def finish(self: Self) -> None:
    """End the silence: music the silencer paused plays on, unless the game paused it last."""
    self.stop_following_music()
    self._spared_sounds = {}
    if (
        self._paused_music
        and not self._game_paused_music
        and pygame.mixer.get_init() is not None
    ):
        # pygame's own unpause: other silencers still following must not take it for the
        # game's
        _MUSIC_FOLLOWING.pygame_unpause()()
    self._paused_music = False

def silence_frame(self: Self) -> None:
    """Stop every sound the silent frame just run started, and pause any music.

    Music the silencer paused plays on at ``finish``. Nothing happens without a mixer.
    """
    if pygame.mixer.get_init() is None:
        return
    if self.spares_playing_sounds:
        self._stop_unspared_channels()
    else:
        pygame.mixer.stop()
    if pygame.mixer.music.get_busy():
        # pygame's own pause: the silencer's, not the game's
        _MUSIC_FOLLOWING.pygame_pause()()
        self._paused_music = True

def relaunch_replay(
    *, command: Sequence[str], handoff_path: Path | None, result_exit_code: int
) -> int:
    """Perform a restart: hand it to the supervisor, or supervise the restarted replays.

    Called once this replay's run is over and torn down (module docstring, step 3).

    Args:
        command: The restart's command (``restart_command``).
        handoff_path: The supervisor's handoff file when this replay is a supervised child
            (``ReplayOptions.restart_handoff_path``), or None in the first replay process.
        result_exit_code: The exit code this replay's own result has
            (``ReplayResult.exit_code``).

    Returns:
        The status this process exits with: ``ExitCode.SUCCESS`` once a supervised child has
        handed its restart over; for the supervisor, the last restarted replay's status (128 +
        N for one killed by signal N) or, when that is ``SUCCESS``, the first non-success result
        of an earlier run; ``ExitCode.INTERRUPTED`` after Ctrl-C, ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR``
        when a child cannot start or its handoff cannot be read, or when this supervised
        child cannot write its handoff.

    """
    handoff = RestartHandoff(command=list(command), result_exit_code=result_exit_code)
    if handoff_path is not None:
        try:
            # Moved into place whole: the supervisor never reads half a handoff
            write_aside_then_replace(
                destination=handoff_path,
                write=lambda aside: aside.write_text(handoff.model_dump_json(), encoding='utf-8'),
            )
        except OSError:
            # Not exit 1 (REPLAY_DIVERGED), which the supervisor would report as a divergence
            LOG.exception('Cannot hand the restart over to the supervising replay')
            return ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR
        return ExitCode.SUCCESS
    # The children write to the same streams: this process's output comes first
    sys.stdout.flush()
    sys.stderr.flush()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='glitchygames-replay-restart-') as directory:
        try:
            return _supervise(
                first_handoff=handoff, handoff_path=Path(directory) / RESTART_HANDOFF_FILE_NAME
            )
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            # The child got the same Ctrl-C and ended (subprocess.run waits briefly, then kills)
            return ExitCode.INTERRUPTED

def restart_command(
    *,
    original: Sequence[str],
    recording_path: Path,
    pause_at_frame: int,
    debug_overlay_visible: bool,
    viewer_state: ViewerState | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Return the command that restarts this replay at a pause frame.

    Args:
        original: This process's command line (``sys.orig_argv``: the interpreter, its options,
            the game and its arguments).
        recording_path: The recording the restart replays (``--replay-trace``).
        pause_at_frame: The frame the restart pauses at (``--replay-pause-at-frame``).
        debug_overlay_visible: Whether the restart starts with the debug overlay shown.
        viewer_state: The viewer's state to carry over (``--replay-viewer-state``), or None.

    Returns:
        ``original`` without its ``--replay-trace``, ``--replay-pause-at-frame``,
        ``--replay-viewer-state``, ``--debug-overlay`` and ``--no-debug-overlay``, then
        ``--debug-overlay`` or ``--no-debug-overlay``, the viewer state when given, and
        ``--replay-trace recording_path --replay-pause-at-frame pause_at_frame``, all before
        any bare ``--``. Every other argument is kept in order.

    """
    command = list(original)
    for option, takes_value in (
        (REPLAY_TRACE_OPTION, True),
        (PAUSE_AT_FRAME_OPTION, True),
        (VIEWER_STATE_OPTION, True),
        (DEBUG_OVERLAY_OPTION, False),
        (NO_DEBUG_OVERLAY_OPTION, False),
    ):
        command = without_option(arguments=command, option=option, takes_value=takes_value)
    appended = [DEBUG_OVERLAY_OPTION if debug_overlay_visible else NO_DEBUG_OVERLAY_OPTION]
    if viewer_state is not None:
        appended += [VIEWER_STATE_OPTION, viewer_state.model_dump_json()]
    appended += [
        REPLAY_TRACE_OPTION,
        str(recording_path),
        PAUSE_AT_FRAME_OPTION,
        str(pause_at_frame),
    ]
    return with_options_appended(arguments=command, appended=appended)

silence #

Run frames in silence: a rebuild's frames and an instant replay's fast-forward.

Frames that run but are not shown (a restarted replay rebuilding up to its pause frame, glitchygames/replay/rebuild.py; an instant replay fast-forwarding to the seconds it shows, glitchygames/replay/playback.py) must not be heard either. FrameSilencer is the one code path both use:

  1. begin follows the game's own pygame.mixer.music.pause() and unpause() calls, so music the game paused itself stays paused at the end. With spares_playing_sounds it also notes the sound each busy channel plays then (the live game's, playing on under a scope).
  2. silence_frame, after each silent frame, stops every sound the frame started (a channel's stop(): Sound.play() gives its channel full volume again, so lowering volumes would not do) and pauses the music. Without spares_playing_sounds every channel is stopped (pygame.mixer.stop(), the rebuild's way: nothing of the live game plays under it). With it, a channel still playing the sound noted at begin plays on; a channel that went idle or plays another sound loses its note and is stopped. A live voice (glitchygames/audio/live.py) queues a new chunk every 100 ms, so its channel soon plays another sound and is stopped, as without sparing.
  3. finish stops following the music controls and resumes the music it paused, unless the game's last call paused it.

Silencers may stack (a fast-forward inside a rebuild): one pair of wrappers replaces pygame's pause and unpause while any silencer follows them. The wrappers tell every following silencer about the game's call and then call pygame's own functions, captured once when the first silencer began; the last silencer to stop puts pygame's functions back, provided the wrappers are still in place (code that replaced them since keeps its own). A silencer's own pause and resume always call pygame's functions, never the wrappers, so no silencer takes another's for the game's.

A game that asks the mixer what is playing (get_busy, Channel.get_busy) may get a different answer during silent frames than when they were recorded; audio is played, never compared, so a replay is unaffected unless game logic depends on it (which no recording could replay exactly anyway). Nothing happens without a mixer.

class FrameSilencer:
    """Keeps frames silent while they run unseen (see the module docstring)."""

    def __init__(self: Self, *, spares_playing_sounds: bool = False) -> None:
        """Start with nothing silenced and the game's music controls not followed.

        Args:
            spares_playing_sounds: True to let the sounds playing at ``begin`` play on (an
                instant replay's fast-forward); False to stop every sound (a rebuild).

        """
        self.spares_playing_sounds = spares_playing_sounds
        # True while music is paused by the silencer (silence_frame), not by the game
        self._paused_music = False
        # Whether the game's last music.pause() / unpause() call while followed paused it
        self._game_paused_music = False
        self._is_following_music = False
        # Channel index -> the sound it played at begin (spares_playing_sounds)
        self._spared_sounds: dict[int, pygame.mixer.Sound] = {}

    def begin(self: Self) -> None:
        """Follow the game's music controls; note the sounds playing (``spares_playing_sounds``).

        Until ``finish`` (or ``stop_following_music``), the game's ``pause`` and ``unpause``
        calls are noted, so ``finish`` resumes music only when the game did not pause it
        itself. A game that bound the functions before (``from pygame.mixer.music import
        pause``) is not followed. Again: nothing.
        """
        if self._is_following_music:
            return
        self._is_following_music = True
        _MUSIC_FOLLOWING.add(silencer=self)
        if self.spares_playing_sounds and pygame.mixer.get_init() is not None:
            for channel_index in range(pygame.mixer.get_num_channels()):
                playing_sound = pygame.mixer.Channel(channel_index).get_sound()
                if playing_sound is not None:
                    self._spared_sounds[channel_index] = playing_sound

    def note_game_music_pause(self: Self, *, paused: bool) -> None:
        """Note the game's own music pause (True) or resume (False), while followed.

        Args:
            paused: Whether the game's call paused the music.

        """
        self._game_paused_music = paused

    def stop_following_music(self: Self) -> None:
        """Stop following the game's music controls (``begin``)."""
        if not self._is_following_music:
            return
        self._is_following_music = False
        _MUSIC_FOLLOWING.remove(silencer=self)

    def silence_frame(self: Self) -> None:
        """Stop every sound the silent frame just run started, and pause any music.

        Music the silencer paused plays on at ``finish``. Nothing happens without a mixer.
        """
        if pygame.mixer.get_init() is None:
            return
        if self.spares_playing_sounds:
            self._stop_unspared_channels()
        else:
            pygame.mixer.stop()
        if pygame.mixer.music.get_busy():
            # pygame's own pause: the silencer's, not the game's
            _MUSIC_FOLLOWING.pygame_pause()()
            self._paused_music = True

    def _stop_unspared_channels(self: Self) -> None:
        """Stop each busy channel not still playing the sound it played at ``begin``."""
        for channel_index in range(pygame.mixer.get_num_channels()):
            channel = pygame.mixer.Channel(channel_index)
            spared_sound = self._spared_sounds.get(channel_index)
            if not channel.get_busy():
                self._spared_sounds.pop(channel_index, None)
            elif spared_sound is None or channel.get_sound() is not spared_sound:
                self._spared_sounds.pop(channel_index, None)
                channel.stop()

    def finish(self: Self) -> None:
        """End the silence: music the silencer paused plays on, unless the game paused it last."""
        self.stop_following_music()
        self._spared_sounds = {}
        if (
            self._paused_music
            and not self._game_paused_music
            and pygame.mixer.get_init() is not None
        ):
            # pygame's own unpause: other silencers still following must not take it for the
            # game's
            _MUSIC_FOLLOWING.pygame_unpause()()
        self._paused_music = False
